LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Here's how to watch, what to know, and an expert prediction before the Pats and Bears face off in Chicago Getty Images In the Week 7 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Chicago Bears play host to the New England Patriots . Chicago is coming off a win in Caleb Williams ' return to the lineup, having held on for a 31-23 victory in a game that moved the Bears to 4-2 on the season. The Bears bounced back from their dispiriting loss to the division rival Green Bay Packers the week before, when the offense looked like a disaster with backup Tyson Bagent under center. Chicago will look to keep the good times rolling here. New England also won what -- on the surface -- looked like a close game against the New York Jets , but finished with a seven-point margin of victory thanks only to a late field goal. The Patriots have won three consecutive games after starting the season 1-2, and their quarterback has found a groove after looking nearly broken to start the year. The Pats, too, are looking to keep the train on the tracks on Thursday night. Will the Bears capture another win, or will the Patriots continue their hot streak? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Bears vs. Patriots live Date: Thursday, Oct. 22 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Soldier Field (Chicago) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bears -3, O/U 50.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Patriots have the ball Drake Maye has found himself over the last three weeks, completing 66 of 103 passes for 878 yards, 10 touchdowns, and one interception after going just 51-of-80 for 585 yards, one touchdown, and six picks through the first three games of the season. Maye has rediscovered the deep ball, in particular, going 12 of 20 for 350 yards and four scores on throws beyond 15 yards in the last three games, per Tru Media. Before that, he was just 9 of 20 for 281 yards and four interceptions on those throws. Maye finished with a strong game against the Jets despite A.J. Brown looking horrifyingly bad in his return from an ankle injury. Brown dropped (at least) three passes and turned his 10 targets into only 27 yards. Maye also lost Romeo Doubs to a shoulder injury on an early-game touchdown pass, so he was working with a limited receiving corps behind Brown. Still, he threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns without turning the ball over. Brown will presumably be better here, and Chicago hasn't been great against outside receivers, but last week's return of Kyler Gordon could lead to slot man Demario Douglas having a tougher go of things than he has over the last few weeks. Kyle Williams could get in on the action with Doubs sidelined, though Efton Chism has been getting more snaps because the Patriots trust him as a blocker. Chicago checks in a surprising eighth in opponents' EPA per dropback so far this season, per Tru Media, thanks to a high sack rate and a few timely interceptions. Opponents have averaged 8.4 yards per attempt against the Bears, though, indicating that you can indeed move the ball through the air if you can get a pass off and avoid a turnover. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has generated pressure at an above-average rate (39.7% of dropbacks) despite working with a somewhat limited group up front, and the Patriots will be without two starting guards here. So, the running backs (particularly Rhamondre Stevenson ) will have to be on their game in pass protection on Thursday night. The Patriots have struggled to run the ball thus far this season, with Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner combining for an average of just 3.9 yards per carry on 151 rushing attempts. Stevenson leads the way in the backfield largely because the Patriots trust him the most in short yardage and pass protection, but he hasn't been efficient or explosive. Henderson had an explosive rushing touchdown on his first run of the season but has failed to record one since. Kiner was a little-used third-stringer until he salted away the game against the Jets last Sunday. He could perhaps work his way into more touches after a nice showing in that game, given the rushing struggles of the two leads and the fact that Henderson also fumbled against New York. The Bears have allowed opponents 4.4 yards per carry on running-back rushes so far this season, with much of the success coming by way of yards before contact. It may be difficult for the Patriots to generate those types of yards with their injury issues along the offensive line, and their backs haven't exactly done the best job of breaking tackles this year, so the challenge of moving the offense down the field will likely fall squarely on Maye's right shoulder. When the Bears have the ball Caleb Williams returned last week from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury and looked no worse for wear. Williams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown. The Bears kept things simple for him with a 3.9-yard average depth of throw (eighth-lowest for any quarterback in a single game this season), per Tru Media, and he was extremely efficient as a result. Williams has only played in three games so far this year, but he's leading the league with a 72.5% completion rate and is up to a career-best 7.8 yards per attempt. And that's despite a truly awful game against the Vikings in Week 2, where he went 15-of-26 for just 138 yards and an interception. In his first couple of appearances, it seemed like journeyman wideout Kalif Raymond (14 targets in Weeks 1 and 2) was his primary option, but on Sunday, it was Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland -- the most expected options -- leading the way with eight and seven targets, respectively. Rome Odunze saw five looks. Given the way they're each deployed, it seems likely that Odunze will see a bunch of Christian Gonzalez 's coverage on Thursday night -- especially with Carlton Davis III ruled out. Odunze is the biggest of the trio and plays most often on the perimeter, and he also tends to run the most routes. If that's the way things go, we should expect the passing game to flow through Burden and Loveland yet again. The Patriots have allowed opponents to complete 31 of 46 passes for 301 yards on throws to the slot this season, per Tru Media. Burden could have a nice night working inside if he's on the field more often than he was last week (eight targets on only 18 routes), though Marcus Jones does have an interception this season and is allowing only 1.46 yards per coverage snap in the slot, per Pro Football Focus. By contrast, New England has allowed only 29 catches for 279 yards to tight ends to date, so Loveland may not find the coverage as friendly. The Bears would do well to line him up all over the formation rather than solely in line, and perhaps use multi-tight end sets where he plays more of a receiver role, and Cole Kmet or Sam Roush handles the blocking aspects of the position. The Bears also tried against Atlanta to do what they do best: run the ball with volume. D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson (the latter filling in for the injured Kyle Monangai ) combined for 29 carries. They ran for only 96 yards on those totes, but they did find the end zone three times. Chicago's offensive line actually created some nice push, generating 1.45 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, but the backs slumped to only 1.83 yards after contact, as they combined for only four broken tackles. (For context, consider that the Seahawks ' running backs combined for 10 in their awful game against the Broncos on Thursday night.) The Pats have allowed only 3.9 yards per rush this season, thanks in part to yielding an average of only 0.75 yards before contact. Swift and Johnson (Monangai is out again) will have to do a better job of breaking tackles this time around if they want to generate yardage and create favorable down-and-distance scenarios for Williams and the passing game. I see this being a high-scoring game, what with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. Maybe Green Bay can actually run with some efficiency in Josh Jacobs ' potential return, but it's not like he was all that efficient last season, either. Pittsburgh is 4-2 after a 26-19 overtime win over Tampa Bay, while New Orleans is 2-4 after beating the Giants 34-27. Kickoff is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET. With both teams coming off big wins in Week 6, let's take a look at the matchup and the bold predictions for Week 7 in Paris, France. Chris Boswell kicks five field goals, two from 50-plus © Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images Boswell is 13-for-17 on field goals this season, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards. Against Tampa Bay he went 4-for-5, with makes from 52 and 58 yards. That was his second straight game with multiple field goals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) New Orleans allows 29.7 points and 377.7 yards per game. Those numbers suggest Pittsburgh will move the ball. Some of those drives will stall before the end zone, and that is where Boswell scores. The prediction goes beyond another solid outing. Boswell makes five field goals, including two from beyond 50 yards. The limitation is his four misses this season, which show he is not automatic from long range. Tyler Shough throws two interceptions Shough has a 12:5 touchdown-to-interception ratio through six games. He threw only 144 yards against the Giants, though he scored four touchdowns in total. He is also playing through broken bones in his non-throwing hand, which may explain why he has just 242 passing yards over the last two weeks. Predicting two interceptions means Shough nearly matches his early-season total in one afternoon. The route to that outcome is straightforward. Pittsburgh's lead will push New Orleans into longer passing situations, and an injured hand makes tight-window throws harder. The call is that one pass is tipped and picked off in the second half, while another is forced into coverage on a late drive. Those turnovers would turn a competitive game into a Steelers cushion. There is a counterpoint. Shough has produced touchdowns despite modest yardage, so this prediction depends on game script more than on his recent efficiency. Chris Olave posts 120 yards and two touchdowns in a losing rally Olave had double-digit targets in each of the first four games. Over the last two he has seen only 13 targets, producing an 8-89-1 line. That drop in volume looks like the sort of dip that corrects itself. Pittsburgh's defense will give him room to correct it. New Orleans' opponents have averaged 256.0 passing yards per game, which suggests quarterbacks can find openings in this matchup. Rookie Germie Bernard's 11-catch, 87-yard, one-touchdown game against the Steelers' last opponent shows how that kind of volume can arise. Olave reaches 10 targets, 120 yards and two touchdowns as New Orleans chases points. Those scores help the Saints cut a two-score deficit to three points late in the fourth quarter. Pittsburgh still holds on. The prediction is Steelers 31, Saints 27, with Boswell's late field goal sealing it. If Jordyn Tyson makes his debut after traveling with the team while recovering from a hamstring injury, the Saints' receiving group could be even more dangerous. These are deliberately high-variance predictions, not the most likely outcomes. The underlying numbers favor Pittsburgh, but turnovers and a motivated passing offense can make this matchup less predictable than the records suggest. For the first time in the league's long existence, a regular season game will be played in France. Paris, to be exact. After nearly 20 years since the Dolphins and Giants played the first regular season game outside of North America, the NFL's international footprint grows larger every year. As interesting as all of that is, the football played on the field is what really matters. Pittsburgh enters Week 7 with a 4-2 record, barely beating the Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime a week ago. The Saints, meanwhile, climbed to 2-4 after a bizarre 34-27 win over the Giants. Both teams have plenty of flaws they are hoping to correct as the season goes on, but the Steelers are favored for a reason. As the game approaches, we will have all of the important details you need to know. Injury reports, weather reports, how to watch, storylines, and more. So bookmark this page and come back throughout the week! How to Watch Pittsburgh Steelers vs New Orleans Saints in Week 7 Date: Sunday, October 25 Time: 9:30 a.m. EST TV Network: NFL Network Announcers: Dave Pasch (Play-by-Play), Kurt Warner and Jason Kelce (Color Analysts), Molly McGrath (Sideline Reporter) Pittsburgh Steelers Injury Report for Week 7 Steelers injury reports will appear here as they become available New Orleans Saints Injury Report for Week 7 Saints injury reports will appear here as they become available Weather Forecast for Pittsburgh Steelers vs New Orleans Saints Week 7 Current Forecast ( via NFLWeather.com ) Temperature: TBD Wind Speed: TBD Precipitation: TBD Biggest Pittsburgh Steelers Storylines heading into Week 7 Will the Steelers continue leaning on the passing game despite missing multiple playmakers? Despite missing multiple receivers heading into their Week 6 matchup with the Buccaneers, the Steelers chose to make the passing game the focal point of the offense. While they ultimately came away with the victory, it was an ugly mess for much of the contest. Aaron Rodgers put up a solid 253 yards through the air, but it took him a whopping 49 pass attempts to get there. He was the definition of a checkdown merchant , with just five of those 49 passes traveling beyond 10 yards, according to Next Gen Stats . It seemed as though Mike McCarthy didn't have faith that Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle could succeed against the Buccaneers' stout run defense. Still, the Steelers can't win games against good teams with that offensive approach. The Saints could be a team that they can once again get away with it against, but it's something to monitor. Which team will handle the international trip better? There has been plenty of discourse surrounding how to handle playing across the pond ever since the NFL's International Series took shape. We saw the Rams be criticized for arriving in Australia right before their Week 1 disaster against the 49ers, who had been down under for days at that point. In the Steelers case, they are taking the route of trying to make the week feel as normal as possible, choosing to fly out on Thursday evening. Meanwhile, the Saints arrived in France on Monday, so they will be well adjusted by game time on Sunday. Will the contrasting strategies make any difference? Only time will tell. Can the Steelers pass rush come alive against a struggling Saints offensive line? The Steelers' pass rush has long been the strength of their defense, but they haven't been as effective on a down-to-down basis this season. According to Sumer Sports , Pittsburgh ranks just 23rd in pressure percentage at 37.4%. They do rank ninth in sacks with 16, so they have managed to get the QB on the ground at an above-average level. Still, they aren't causing as much disruption as they need to be, considering the names in that group. T.J. Watt has cooled off after a hot start, Alex Highsmith isn't having his best season, and Nick Herbig has made splash plays but hasn't been as dominant as he was last season. The interior has been hot and cold, with Cam Heyward remaining a consistent presence while the other pieces have been hit-or-miss. With the Saints missing star left tackle Kaleb Banks, this is an opportunity for them to really hit their stride. If they don't, it may be time to worry. picks.blurb: Week 7 odds: Steelers open as slight favorites vs. Saints - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview Week 7 odds: Steelers open as slight favorites vs. Saints (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jason Aponte Tue, October 20, 2026 at 2:30 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers are coming off a tough road win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. The AFC North race is heating up, and as crazy as it sounds, the Cleveland Browns lead the division, something nobody could have predicted before the season. The entire division is over .500, and three teams are 4-2. Every game is critical, and the Steelers look to continue their winning streak with a win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris, France. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Steelers open as three-point favorites despite the neutral site. The Saints are coming off a victory of their own after a furious comeback attempt by the New York Giants, and J.J. McCarthy fell just short. The over/under is 44.5, and Steelers moneyline odds sit at -174. The line will move with injury news from both teams, but this feels right. On the one hand, the Saints offense is a handful, but the defense, aside from Chase Young and a few other players, is vulnerable. The key will be getting off to a faster start on offense and defense. At the beginning of the Tampa Bay game and for much of the game, the Steelers felt stuck in neutral. The offense and defense kicked it into gear down the stretch and snatched victory from the jaws of defeat. Rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard was fantastic and has quickly earned the trust of Aaron Rodgers. Trust me, that isn't easy to earn. Rodgers and Bernard looked like Rodgers and Cobb from the Packers days. D.K. Metcalf turned in a big game and made critical plays down the stretch. While the receiver room gets healthy, the two receivers will need to continue making plays. Jaylen Warren slowed down off his torrid pace, but Rico Dowdle was effective on Sunday. Still, at the end of the game, Warren was the one making big plays in overtime. It's the NFL and every game is difficult, but the Steelers need this one and Vegas believes they will get it done. picks.headline: Saints vs. Steelers Prediction: Bonjour de Paris
picks.blurb: Saints vs. Steelers Prediction: Bonjour de Paris - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview Saints vs. Steelers Prediction: Bonjour de Paris Tina Howell Fri, October 23, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New Orleans Saints are overseas this week for a historic matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday, October 25, at Stade de France in Paris. The Week 7 game marks the NFL's first regular-season game in France, giving both franchises an opportunity to make history on an international stage. However, for the Saints, the trip represents something more important: a chance to build momentum and potentially turn their season around. New Orleans enters Sunday's matchup at 2-4 after a much-needed 34-27 victory over the New York Giants, which snapped their three-game losing streak. Meanwhile, Aaron Rogers and the 4-2 Steelers arrive in Paris riding the momentum of a 26-19 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. With their bye week approaching, the Saints have an opportunity to string together consecutive victories for the first time this season and return home with renewed confidence. However, Tyler Shough and the offense will face a challenging Pittsburgh defense that ranks 9th in total defense, allowing just 307.5 yards per game. The Steelers have also been effective against the pass, surrendering an average of 204.3 passing yards per contest. PREDICTION: Saints 31 – Steelers 27 Yes, the Saints have an opportunity to make history in Paris, but the bigger question is whether they can turn one encouraging victory into sustained success. Following last week's comments from team owner Gayle Benson, the pressure is mounting on both players and coaches to deliver results. Add in the spotlight of an international stage and Sunday's matchup against the Steelers becomes even more significant. I believe the Saints will win this game but more importantly, Sunday will provide a clearer picture of whether the Saints are finally finding their footing after a slow start to the season or if the team still has more questions than answers. picks.headline: Steelers RB picks up a new injury ahead of Week 7 Paris game vs. Saints
picks.blurb: Steelers RB picks up a new injury ahead of Week 7 Paris game vs. Saints - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview Steelers RB picks up a new injury ahead of Week 7 Paris game vs. Saints Andrew Vasquez, Steelers Wire Thu, October 22, 2026 at 3:45 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads As soon as Pittsburgh Steelers running back Rico Dowdle got over a concerning injury he suffered early this season, a surprise health setback popped up just days before the Week 7 Paris game against the New Orleans Saints . Courtesy of the team's Week 7 practice report, the Steelers revealed that Dowdle was limited with a new knee injury. The severity of the surprise setback and when he suffered the injury are unknown, but his limited participation is worth something. Dowdle, who signed with the Steelers in March 2026, was coming off consecutive 1,000-yard seasons with two different teams: the Dallas Cowboys (2024) and Carolina Panthers (2025). A third consecutive 1,000-yard season with Pittsburgh would make Dowdle the first running back in history to do so with three different teams, but injuries have made achieving the feat more difficult. Oh, and Jaylen Warren's emergence certainly didn't make it easier. We at Steelers Wire will monitor Dowdle's status moving forward, with his practice availability on Thursday and Friday giving us a better idea of whether or not he can suit up in Week 7. away.headline: Steelers' TJ Watt pops up on injury report with new concern
away.blurb: The former Defensive Player of the Year didn’t practice on Wednesday for a rest designation. But, then he was limited in practice on Thursday because of a calf injury. This is a new injury to the public. There was some good defensive news coming out of the Steelers’ injury report, though. Cornerback Jalen Ramsey was limited on Thursday after not practicing the day prior with a wrist injury, so that was improvement. Outside linebacker Alex Highsmith was also limited with a groin issue, the same designation as Wednesday. Related Articles Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Pittsburgh Steelers haven’t been able to catch a break from injuries the last few weeks. It seems like a new star player is being added to the injury report each week. Thursday’s injury report included a surprising name, one that Steelers fans wish wasn’t on the list: edge rusher T.J. Watt. It’s unclear when or how Watt suffered the calf injury. But, now there’s a possibility, even if just a slight one, that Watt could miss Sunday’s game in Paris against the New Orleans Saints . Watt being absent for a game is always a loss for the Steelers. He can always make big and important plays for his team. Through six games this season, Watt’s recorded 4.5 sacks (tied for eighth in the league), 15 tackles, one interception, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery. Veteran tackle Cameron Heyward didn’t practice Wednesday or Thursday for rest designations, but he should be good to go come Sunday. Safety DeShon Elliott recorded his second-straight full practice on Thursday, meaning he’ll likely play on Sunday. It would mark Elliott’s first game since last October after he suffered an MCL sprain, hyperextended knee and a hamstring injury. away.blurb: Seeing the Eagles be viewed as a team that could target Rudolph is understandable. With Hurts being out long-term, the Eagles would benefit by adding another quarterback with NFL experience to their depth. While Rudolph is not a star like Hurts, he would give Philadelphia another QB option to work with as they aim to get their season back on track. Philadelphia Eagles star quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to be done for the season after being diagnosed with blood clots in both his lungs and deep vein thrombosis. Now, with Hurts done for the year, the Eagles are being linked to a trade for a Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback. In a recent article for Bleacher Report , Kristopher Knox named the Eagles as a potential suitor for Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph. "Mason Rudolph remains the most logical trade target for teams seeking a backup quarterback or spot starter midseason. He's one of three reserve QBs that the Pittsburgh Steelers have behind Aaron Rodgers, along with Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar," Knox wrote. "Potential Suitors : Miami Dolphins, Philadelphia Eagles." Rudolph is currently in his seventh NFL season and sixth with the Steelers. In 36 career NFL games split between the Steelers and Tennessee Titans, he has thrown 30 touchdowns, 22 interceptions, 4,925 passing yards, and has completed 64.3% of his passes. He has primarily been a backup quarterback during his career and could be a solid player for the Eagles to add to their group ahead of the deadline.

away.headline: Steelers week 7 final injury report: game status
away.blurb: The Saints currently sit third in the NFC South, just 1.5 games out of first place. Meanwhile, the Steelers are only half a game behind the division leaders in the AFC North. Both teams also have injury concerns heading into Sunday’s matchup. Pittsburgh could get some key players back in the coming weeks, but several injured contributors may not return until after the bye. The Steelers will face a significant test as they manage those injuries and look to overcome their road struggles. The Steelers will be without wide receiver Skowronek and cornerback Echols against the Saints after both missed all three practices. Running back Dowdle remains questionable after three consecutive limited sessions, while safety Elliott is also questionable despite practicing fully throughout the week as he works toward a return from injured reserve. The Pittsburgh Steelers are headed to Paris to take on the New Orleans Saints in the NFL’s first-ever game in France . Pittsburgh has an opportunity to strengthen its position in the AFC North before heading into its bye week. However, both teams have plenty at stake as they navigate tight divisional races early in the season. Pittsburgh received a boost with Watt, Ramsey, and Highsmith all progressing to full participation Friday and listed as in. Their availability strengthens the Steelers’ defense heading into Sunday’s matchup in Paris. away.headline: Steelers Could Be Without Key Offensive Weapon vs. Saints
away.blurb: Pittsburgh Steelers running back Rico Dowdle (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints in Paris. Dowdle was listed as a limited participant in practice for the second straight day on Thursday, Oct. 22 with a knee injury. Dowdle was first listed as a limited participant in practice on Wednesday, Oct. 21 with the knee injury. Dowdle was also an estimated limited practice participant on Friday. The Steelers cancelled Friday's practice in Paris due to rain and wind in the forecast. Dowdle played against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, Oct. 18 after being listed as questionable with a toe injury. Dowdle missed three consecutive games after suffering the toe injury in the team's Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots. Steelers Could Be Without Key Offensive Weapon vs. Saints - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Steelers Could Be Without Key Offensive Weapon vs. Saints Pittsburgh Steelers running back Rico Dowdle at practice on Oct. 8, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Chris Ward Fri, October 23, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Travis Homer replaced Dowdle in the rotation at running back with Jaylen Warren . Dowdle joined the Steelers with plans of splitting the workload with Jaylen Warren, who has emerged as Pittsburgh's top ball carrier this season. "He's been very underrated in this league for a long time," tight end Pat Freiermuth said of Warren after a 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 4. "I go back to when PQ (Patrick Queen) was in Baltimore and he came here, I'm pretty sure he said when Jaylen was a rookie (or in his) second-year, that he's the hardest to tackle in the NFL. … Every time we get him the ball, he makes a good play." Still, the Steelers will need to keep Warren fresh if they want him to be effective late into the season. Dowdle being in the fold helps that. Dowdle rushed for 40 yards on seven carries (5.7 average) in Sunday's overtime win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. home.headline: Saints Injury Report: Cesar Ruiz out again Thursday ahead of Steelers game
home.blurb: Saints Injury Report: Cesar Ruiz out again Thursday ahead of Steelers game – Crescent City Sports menu The New Orleans Saints continued preparations for Sunday's matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris on Thursday, with starting right guard Cesar Ruiz remaining sidelined by a knee injury and kicker Daniel Carlson still absent for personal reasons. Ruiz, who sustained the injury during Sunday's 34-27 victory over the New York Giants, did not participate in Thursday's practice after also missing Wednesday's session. His availability is a significant concern for a Saints offensive line preparing to face Pittsburgh's defensive front in Paris. Carlson also missed another practice after not traveling with the Saints to France. Instead, he awaits the arrival of his newborn child. Head coach Kellen Moore previously indicated that the kicker was expected to join the team before Sunday's game. Practice squad kicker Charlie Smyth remains a potential option if Carlson cannot return in time. The Saints added defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to Thursday's report as a non-injury-related rest designation. He did not practice. There was encouraging news elsewhere on the injury report. Quarterback Tyler Shough continued to participate fully despite dealing with a left-hand injury. Backup quarterback Spencer Rattler, who was added to the report with a knee injury Thursday, also practiced fully. Running back C.J. Donaldson was upgraded to full participation after being limited Wednesday with a shoulder injury. Cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry (head) and defensive tackle Nathan Shepherd (illness) also practiced fully. Linebackers Anfernee Jennings (knee) and Kaden Elliss (calf) remained limited, as did running back Alvin Kamara, who is managing a back injury. Elliss' potential return would be particularly important as the linebacker has missed the previous three games while dealing with the calf injury. He has expressed optimism about playing against Pittsburgh. More clarity should come on Friday with the final injury report. The Week 7 game is apoears to be pivotal. Entering the bye week 3-4 and on a win streak versus 2-5 may the difference for New Orleans between making a push in the NFC South or a disappointing campaign. The Saints face the Steelers on Sunday at Stade de France, with kickoff scheduled for 8:30 a.m. Central time in part of the NFL's international series. home.headline: ‘I Hate Poorly Ran Organizations’ — Former Steelers DT Slams Pittsburgh’s Questionable Travel Plan for Paris Game vs. Saints
home.blurb: In a scathing post on X, Fehoko pointed out the Saints’ opposite approach and slammed the Steelers, revealing that players did not sleep on overnight flights. “This is one of the dumbest things I’ve ever seen. Every NFL plane ride is pure card games, movie watching, and guys hanging out. Thinking that “they’ll sleep overnight” on the plane is so stupid. The Saints are already in Paris getting acclimated. I hate poorly ran organizations,” Fehoko wrote . The issue of different teams’ travel schedules reared its head when the Los Angeles Rams arrived in Australia less than 30 hours before kickoff, while the 49ers had arrived roughly a week earlier to acclimate. The 49ers look well rested as they blew out the sluggish Rams 27-7 at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in front of 100,021 fans, the seventh-largest attendance in NFL history. The Pittsburgh Steelers improved to 4-2 on the season after a thrilling overtime 26-19 Week 6 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on the road. Next up, the Steelers will travel to Paris, France, for a Week 7 clash against the New Orleans Saints at Stade De France. Former Steelers defensive tackle Breiden Fehoko slammed the franchise after it was revealed that the team will take a red-eye flight to Paris on Thursday evening and go straight to training after landing. Breiden Fehoko Takes Issue With Steelers’ Paris Travel Plans PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Later, Rams coach Sean McVay took responsibility for the team’s unusual travel arrangements, while the 49ers were praised for adapting to the 17-hour time difference and acclimating more quickly. The 27-7 scoreline prompted the NFL to consider adopting a standardized travel timeline for international games, rather than leaving it to teams. The Steelers’ Week 7 clash against the Saints will also be held during a storm of protests that have gripped France in recent days. During this week’s segment of the “Christian Kuntz” podcast, Pittsburgh long snapper Christian Kuntz revealed that league officials had reassured the players of their safety during their stay in Paris. “We had an NFL security meeting. Which, I’m sure every team when you travel overseas, you have a meeting,” Kuntz said. “Basically, they told us that, ‘Yeah, there’s riots going on. This is why they’re rioting. It’s not a threat in our area. We have tripled the security now. Everything’s gonna be fine. Your families are gonna be safe.’ So, they’ve advised us that it’s gonna be safe.” The Steelers are seeking a third straight win after suffering a damaging Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns. Pittsburgh has shown flashes of brilliance on both sides of the ball this season, earning a PFN Team Impact score of 75.5 (No. 14 in the NFL). picks.blurb: Recently Cut Atlanta Falcons 3rd-Round Pick Puts Raheem Morris, 49ers on Alert Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Former Atlanta Falcons edge rusher Bralen Trice is exploring his next opportunity after visiting the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday, less than a week after appearing on Atlanta's active roster. The 49ers hosted Trice for a visit after the Falcons released him on Tuesday, Oct. 20. The former third-round pick is looking for a new home after finally making his NFL regular-season debut in 2026, following two injury-plagued seasons in Atlanta. San Francisco's defensive staff includes former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris, now the 49ers' defensive coordinator. Although Morris coached Atlanta in 2024 and 2025, Trice never played under him in a regular-season game. Trice spent his first two NFL seasons sidelined by injuries while Morris led the Falcons. If Trice joins the 49ers, he would be the second former Falcon Morris has brought to San Francisco. The 49ers signed edge rusher Khalid Kareem from the Falcons' Practice Squad before the season opener. Atlanta selected Trice with the 74th overall pick in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Washington, hoping he could develop into a productive pass rusher. However, his professional career got off to a difficult start when he tore his ACL during his first preseason game as a rookie. Trice missed the entire 2024 season before suffering another setback with the same knee during the 2025 campaign. Those injuries kept him out of a regular-season game during his first two years with the organization. The 25-year-old entered training camp healthy in 2026 but did not make Atlanta's initial 53-man roster. After clearing waivers, he returned to the Falcons' practice squad in early September. Atlanta gave Trice three weeks of practice squad elevations to prove himself. His Week 3 performance against the Green Bay Packers stood out, as he recorded four quarterback hurries while helping Atlanta's defensive front generate pressure. The Falcons eventually signed Trice to their active roster on Oct. 17 after using all three of his standard practice squad elevations. However, his time back on the 53-man roster was brief, as Atlanta released him three days later after the Falcons signed Charles Snowden from the Washington Commanders Practice Squad . Trice appeared in four games for Atlanta this season, recording two total tackles and one pass defended, according to the Falcons' official release announcement and NFL statistics. He also showed flashes as a pass rusher, particularly with his four quarterback hurries against Green Bay. For San Francisco, the visit offers a chance to evaluate a young defender who has faced significant adversity but is finally getting meaningful NFL playing time. His experience working along the defensive front could give the 49ers another option as they assess their depth at linebacker and edge defender. Morris' presence adds an interesting connection between Trice's former team and his potential next destination, even without a previous on-field relationship between the two. Trice has yet to establish himself as a consistent NFL contributor, but his healthy return in 2026 gave him his first chance to show the ability that earned him a third-round selection. Whether that opportunity continues in San Francisco remains to be seen. picks.blurb: Morris is surely equipped to counter Atlanta's attack, having led the same core from 2024-25 as head coach. But a San Francisco defense that tops the league in defensive expected points added per play on rushing attempts will be in for its stiffest test yet against the All-Pro ball carrier. On the other side of the ball, Brock Purdy will look to maintain sky-high efficiency despite mounting attrition at wide receiver . Falcons vs 49ers odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: 49ers -4.5 Moneyline: 49ers -230; Falcons +190 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Falcons vs 49ers USA TODAY expert picks Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: 49ers 35, Falcons 24 How San Francisco's surprising defense handles Robinson is sure to be one of the most compelling storylines in this game. But mitigating any damage might not fall on that unit alone. Chicago managed to minimize Robinson's role by stringing together long drives and holding onto the ball for more than 40 minutes. Given how prolific San Francisco's offense is at working the intermediate area - and how badly Atlanta's defense struggles in that area - the 49ers could leave the Falcons in a problematic position by racing out to an early lead and controlling the terms of the game. Adam Kaufman: 49ers 30, Falcons 23 At some point, San Francisco's injuries have to catch up with it, right? The 49ers keep answering that question with another win to stay unbeaten, although Mike Evans' latest injury creates another challenge on a short week before traveling to Atlanta. Fortunately, Brock Purdy still has Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle to help keep the offense moving. I like those options against a Falcons secondary that has struggled. The Falcons' path is straightforward: feed Bijan Robinson, keep Purdy watching and prevent Michael Penix Jr. from having to rescue the game with difficult throws. That should keep Atlanta competitive, but I'm still expecting San Francisco to execute more consistently and take advantage of a mistake or two. Will McFadden Senior Reporter FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — The Atlanta Falcons will look to break their two-game skid against one of the NFL's three remaining undefeated teams when the San Francisco 49ers come to town for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff on Sunday. Injuries have become a storyline for both teams, particularly for Atlanta's defense and San Francisco's offense, and there could be some important game-time decisions. Nevertheless, there is plenty of familiarity between these coaching staffs and star power on these rosters. As was the case in Week 5, when the Falcons faced the Baltimore Ravens, this game will feature two of the league's preeminent running backs in Bijan Robinson and Christian McCaffrey. The 49ers are also led offensively by quarterback Brock Purdy, who is playing arguably the best football of his career so far this season. "The more you watch him, the more you just appreciate the player that he is," Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich said of Purdy. "He does everything well. And that's the truth. His footwork, he's getting through his progressions, his timing, his accuracy, the velocity he puts on the ball, the touch. And then when it's all said and done, the ability to create when it's not there." Purdy could be missing his top target on Sunday, though, as Mike Evans left the 49ers' last game before halftime due to injury. Atlanta's defense could get a key player of its own back for this one as A.J. Terrell Jr. began practicing this week after spending the last four games on injured reserve due to a groin injury. If both players suit up on Sunday, Terrell and Evans will rekindle a familiar matchup. Here's a look at who the experts predict will win on Sunday between the Falcons and 49ers. away.headline: 49ers injury updates: No major changes on 2nd week 7 practice report
away.blurb: There are a handful of players already ruled out for Week 7, but we could see some players back in action against the Falcons as the 49ers look to get a little healthier in time to go for a 7-0 start to the 2026 campaign. Christian Kirk trending toward return in Week 7 It's not a huge surprise to see optimism about Kirk's return for the 49ers' game in Atlanta. With Mike Evans potentially out because of Achilles tendinitis San Francisco needs reinforcements. Kirk's practice window was opened before Week 6, and now with a second week of practice in it sounds like the club is gearing up for him to come back in Week 7. Head coach Kyle Shanahan on Thursday spoke with KNBR and said Kirk is trending toward making his 2026 debut. " He looked good out there ," Shanahan said. "Talking to him he felt good, and I think he felt good last week. So it's trending in the right direction." The 49ers only open the first portion of practice to media, and neither Bosa nor Evans were on hand for the open part of the session according to reporters on site. Evans is working through Achilles tendonitis. He didn't practice leading up to Week 6 and still suited up before exiting the game late in the second quarter. For Bosa there was optimism he'd be back Thursday. Early indications are he isn't going to participate, but that could change if he comes out after media exit. Kyle Shanahan hopes Nick Bosa will return to practice Thursday Bosa has been out since Week 3 when he suffered a calf injury. The issue wasn't supposed be long-term and there was some hope he'd return for Week 6. Bosa didn't practice at all in Week 6 before being ruled out. He didn't participate in Wednesday's session, but head coach Kyle Shanahan expressed some optimism the star defensive end would be in the team's second practice of the week. "Can't go today, but hoping he'll be out there tomorrow," Shanahan said before practice. There may not be a team in the NFL more in need of a Bye week than the San Francisco 49ers . San Francisco will visit the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7, and then they'll be off for Week 8 where their injury situation could improve dramatically. We'll be keeping a close eye on the 49ers' injury updates all week. Follow along here: 49ers Thursday practice participation report Mike Evans, Nick Bosa not present for early part of Thursday practice Kyle Shanahan won't confirm Mike Evans injury severity There was a report from NFL Media's Ian Rapoport indicating the 49ers would have to manage Evans' Achilles tendonitis throughout the season. Shanahan would neither confirm nor deny that report while speaking with reporters ahead of Wednesday's practice. “We had to manage it last week and we're managing it this week," Shanahan said. "So, we'll see how the rest of the year goes.” It may behoove the 6-0 49ers to let their best pass rusher sit another week and then get the Bye before returning Week 9 at home vs. the Las Vegas Raiders. 49ers Wednesday practice participation report This article

away.blurb: Head coach Kyle Shanahan is doing anything but breathing easy at this point. The 49ers have suffered a slew of injuries that have impacted them throughout the season, and there is no let up as they prepare for the Commanders. They have gotten a dynamic performance from the QB-RB-WR trio of Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and Mike Evans to this point in the season, but Evans is battered and bruised in his first season with the 49ers. He is listed as questionable for the Week 6 Monday night game. He has been battling bruised ribs and now he also has an Achilles issue that kept him out of practice Friday. It would be a major blow if the 49ers did not have him in the lineup against the Commanders. While Shanahan and Purdy have to be prepared for that possibility and have alternatives in mind, Evans will fight to remain in the lineup. “We all know what he’s been playing through, the immense pain that he has every single play,” said 49ers center Jake Brendel , per Matt Barrows of The Athletic . “He still goes out there and does his very best to get a completion for us. It’s fantastic.” Brandin Cooks will be the Niners' primary deep threat in this game, and if Evans can't play or is severely limited, he will become their No. 1 receiver. Cooks has only played in 2 games this season and his numbers are not significant. He has caught just 3-7-1, but that does not mean he would struggle in this game. away.headline: Joey Bosa NFL Comeback Talk? Free agent tipped for 49ers return; speculation links brothers
away.source: The Times of India on MSN
away.blurb: Four months later, that opportunity arose. Isn’t now the best time to return? Also, the big games may be starting soon. He could be that major boost for the 49ers - when they truly need it the most. Joey Bosa retirement rumors have been circulating throughout the 2026 offseason. They may have halted for a second into the season. Get breaking news anytime, anywhere. Download the TOI app now! But with six games played and Nick Bosa missing four of them for the San Francisco 49ers, the rumors are back in action. Only this time, there’s a spice of an NFL comeback, with midseason urgency. Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay has identified Joey Bosa as a potential addition for San Francisco. The 49ers are navigating defensive-line injury concerns; the veteran edge rusher could become an ideal solution for a team looking to strengthen its pass rush during the 2026 NFL season. Joey Bosa’s reunion with Nick Bosa in San Francisco 49ers Nick Bosa’s Week 2 calf injury has severely affected the franchise’s ability to attack quarterbacks from the edge. Signing Nick Bosa’s older brother, Joey Bosa, could help address that weakness. Not just that, but also pursue a forever dream of championship success. The 49ers’ possibility of signing Joey carries more than just professional significance. It also carries a personal touch: the brothers haven’t played together since their high school days. That was in 2012. Their mother, Cheryl Bosa, really hopes to see Joey in a San Francisco 49ers jersey, just like her other son, Nick. Joey is a former Los Angeles Chargers edge defender who represented the Buffalo Bills in 2025. He recorded 5.0 sacks, 5 forced fumbles, 16 quarterback hits, and 9 tackles for loss in 15 games during the 2025 season. He had signed a one-year, $12M contract with the Bills in March 2025. There was no renewal. He didn’t consider a comeback in the 2026 offseason. Nick said that Joey’s more into golf than the NFL. But there was no retirement news either. This leaves the NFL comeback speculation alive and well and doing cyberspace rounds. He was a capable threat in Buffalo last season, and his extensive experience and pass-rushing ability could make him a useful rotational defender if he ever returns to a team that also features his younger brother, Nick. Joey Bosa retirement rumors continue despite NFL interest Across 10 seasons with the Los Angeles Chargers and Buffalo Bills, he recorded 77 sacks and 22 forced fumbles in 122 games. If he could win a Super Bowl alongside his younger brother Nick Bosa, wouldn’t that be the best closing chapter to his NFL career? We can only hope for that to happen. Or maybe he has retired. Can a previously 0-5 squad keep pushing the turnaround and secure their second straight victory? Last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts represented a new wave of promise for the Titans. But in the Browns, Tennessee will face the top team (in a three-way tie) in the AFC North. Cleveland has come on strong, and are coming to Nashville off a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. In the wake of a long-awaited win, I've got one reason the Titans will beat the Browns, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction. Will: Robert Saleh's defense takes over again Robert Saleh's defense just had their best performance of the season. Almost single-handedly, the score-stopping unit bottled up the Colts' offense when it mattered. The Titans forced multiple turnovers and forced Daniel Jones to make mistakes through the air. If Tennessee finds a way to win again this week, it will likely be due to a similar performance from the defense. Expect Saleh to send the heat once again after last week's six-sack outing. PFF has the Browns' offensive line ranked all the way down at 26th in the NFL. If the Titans' defensive line can force Deshaun Watson to unsettle in the pocket, we could be in for a similar path to victory for Tennessee. Won't: Browns get young playmakers going Oppositely, with the Titans' offense still operating at an inconsistent level, this game could get out of hand if Cleveland gets their young playmakers going. Harold Fannin is one of the best rising TEs in the league, too; Cleveland has options, and offensive-minded head coach Todd Monken has led them to a surprising 4-2 tally as a result. Tennessee's defense needs to set the tone early. If the Browns come out swinging, and the Titans' offense takes as long as usual to get into any kind of rhythm, the team could be facing another steep halftime deficit. I just don't like their odds to overcome that two weeks in a row, even if this game is in Nashville. Prediction: Titans win, 17-14 However, I don't believe the Titans will have to worry about that. I'll err to to the positive side with my prediction (something I could be accused of doing too often) and say that Saleh's defense has another big game on the way to a Titans win. This team hasn't won two straight games since Weeks 10 and 11 of the 2022 season. That's a vile streak, but after last week's victory, now feels like the perfect time for Tennessee to break it. Saleh finally has his legs under him as a head coach with this team. The Browns haven't scored more than 13 points in two weeks. In front of a potentially revamped home crowd, the stars are aligning for a home upset for Tennessee. I don't believe the offense will take any major strides, but in Week 7, maybe they won't have to. picks.blurb: 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7 Andrew Harbaugh, Browns Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 2:55 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns march into Week 7 with an AFC North division lead and momentum behind them again. They are starting a softer stretch of the schedule but remain focused on the task ahead, which is the Tennessee Titans. Despite winning their first game in Week 6, the Titans are better than they have played. The Browns can win this game, though, if they keep up their defensive aggressiveness and make significant second-half adjustments. Todd Monken and his staff have risen to the occasion in every game, but this could be their first complete game in 2026 if they execute the way they are capable of. We said this is a poor Titans team, but there is still a game to be played, and we have some bold predictions to share ahead of it. Jared Verse gets his first sack of the season This is a wild thing to think about, but heading into Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans, Jared Verse is without a sack this season. Equally, Myles Garrett has also gone without a sack, but he has been on injured reserve. Fair or unfair, Verse is going to be linked to Garrett, and that means expectations will always be high. The Titans' offensive line is not the best unit, they are going to give up pressures, and it is time for Verse to capitalize on that. Jerry Jeudy finds the endzone Jerry Jeudy has seen him get more and more reps and big-time targets since Week 4 against the Pittsburgh Steelers. In Week 6, he made a pivotal catch-and-run that set up the game-winning field goal by Andre Szmyt. Deshaun Watson and Todd Monken have spoke highly of Jeudy this past week and he seems poised for another boost to his role. In Week 7 against he Titans, he can take advantage of their poor secondary and find the endzone for the first time this season. Browns secure at least five sacks Titans quarterback Cam Ward has had a rough start to the season and it has Tennessee sitting with a record of 1-5. He has a tendency to hold onto the ball, be reckless with it, and I think that has the Browns poised to have a big week on the defensive side of the ball. You cannot always count on turnovers, but you can count on Mike Rutenberg being aggressive on defense. One way he will do that is by getting after Ward, and I think that is where the Browns are most productive in the form of securing at least five sacks. away.headline: Browns new star RB trade target emerges amid injury trouble
away.blurb: The Cleveland Browns are having a good start to the season, as they have a 4-2 record and are at the top of the AFC North. With the way the Browns are playing, it is very likely that they will be buyers ahead of the trade deadline. When looking at the Browns’ current roster, it is clear that they should be looking to add a running back. They have been dealing with injury trouble at the position, so it would not be surprising at all if they acquired a running back by the deadline. Due to this, the Browns are now being connected to a notable running back trade candidate. In a recent article for Bleacher Report , Kristopher Knox named the Browns as the top potential suitor for Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard. “Running back Tony Pollard is a good support piece for Ward right now, but he’s 29 years old and an impending free agent. He should have a solid trade market, though, as he has four 1,000-yard seasons on his resume and could upgrade several of the backfields that have been impacted by injuries this season,” Knox wrote. “Potential Suitors: Cleveland Browns, Seattle Seahawks.” Pollard would certainly be an interesting running back for the Browns to add to their roster as they continue their playoff push. The eight-year NFL veteran would provide Cleveland’s offense with a nice boost, as he is still an impactful player at this stage in his career. In six games this season with the Titans, Pollard has recorded one touchdown, 87 rushes, and 349 rushing yards. He also recorded over 1,000 rushing yards over his previous four seasons. With this, the Pro Bowler would be a significant pickup for the Browns if acquired. It will be interesting to see if they pursue him because of it. home.headline: What Robert Saleh said about Jordan Elliott situation, response from Titans and NFL
home.blurb: "The (defensive line) room is really close," Saleh said. "For JFM to go out there and kind of help Jordan through with whatever he was dealing with at that moment I thought was really admirable on JFM’s part." The incident, which is under review by the NFL, followed a practice altercation with teammate JC Latham. Teammate John Franklin-Myers was credited with de-escalating the situation before it worsened. Tennessee Titans coach Robert Saleh confirmed on Oct. 21 that Jordan Elliott pulled a gun in the team facility's parking lot after a practice altercation last week, leading to the defensive tackle's release this week. An NFL spokesperson told The Tennessean on Oct. 21 that the Titans "promptly" notified the league about the matter, and it is under review. Saleh praised the organization and the NFL's response to the incident, citing a "pause" by the team and the league in getting Elliott assistance for what Saleh called a sign for "a cry for help" instead of involving law enforcement. "And the reason why I think the NFL and the organization did an outstanding job is because this is a man who is father, a great husband. He’s never committed a crime in his entire life," Saleh said. "And he pulled a gun in the parking lot. And the first question that I think everyone forgets to ask is why would a great man, a great father, a man who shows up on time every day, works his ass off every day, contributes the way he's supposed to contribute, is well-liked in the locker room — Why did he go off the rails and grab a gun? "And to me, those are small signs of a cry of help. In terms of, obviously there’s something greater happening. And I thought the team and the NFL did an outstanding job with regards to pausing and asking those questions and checking every single box with regards to getting him the help that he needs." Saleh vouched for Elliott's character despite the incident. The veteran defensive tackle with seven seasons in the NFL played for Saleh in San Francisco last year before joining the Titans in free agency in the spring. "These kids go through a lot. A lot. And... I will stand on the table for Jordan’s character," Saleh said. "Unfortunately, rules are rules with regards to guns on property. And sometimes it’s far greater than the knee-jerk reaction of kicking somebody when they are down. "My message to 31 other teams would be if you need a helluva run-stopping defensive tackle that can help you on a playoff run, give me a call. I’ll tell you everything you need to know about him. He’s a good man. Had a terrible lapse in judgement that I recognize as a call for help more than a criminal act." What happened with Jordan Elliott at the Titans' facility? Elliott attempted to retrieve a gun from his vehicle after a practice altercation with JC Latham on Oct. 15, according to multiple reports. home.headline: Tennessee Titans' Alontae Taylor responds to surprise benching
home.blurb: Tennessee invested heavily in Taylor and projected him as a full-time outside cornerback in the new system, a role he'd take on for the first extended period of his NFL career. That transition hasn't gone smoothly so far, and it appears the “reset” head coach Robert Saleh talks about may include a return to a nickel role. Taylor is clearly frustrated by the decision, though he said he wouldn’t change his decision to join the Titans organization and will keep showing up and doing everything he can to get back in the lineup, while hinting at a possible return to the slot. “Yeah, I was told that I would come here to play corner. Um, and that’s what my mentality was. Um, but now, um, things are changing, and I’ll just adapt," he said, while also pointing out the scheme is “different than anything I’ve played.” Amid talk about Jordan Elliott on Wednesday at the Tennessee Titans facility, cornerback Alontae Taylor sat down to discuss his unexpected inactive-day listing for Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts. Yes, the move would frustrate the Tennessee native, who is now playing for the Titans, but in the long term, it could be the best thing for both Taylor and the Titans. Taylor is a tremendous nickel cornerback, and that role is essential in every NFL defense; those players are hard to find. Time will tell if it was the right decision for Taylor and the organization. Week 7 doesn’t feature a ton of obvious Survivor spots, as the Houston Texans (9.5-point favorites against the New York Giants), Minnesota Vikings (5.5-point favorites against the Colts) and Rams (5.5-point favorites against the Las Vegas Raiders) are the three teams favored by the most on Sunday. NFL Week 6 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Indianapolis Colts (L) Iain MacMillan: New England Patriots (W) It wasn’t a perfect week in these picks, but as always we’ll allow Dewey to “buy back in” so we can share differing perspectives each week in these picks. Week 7 may be the toughest week of the season, as some quality teams (Buffalo, Jacksonville mainly) are on the bye. Washington and the Los Angeles Chargers also won’t play in Week 7. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 7 Survivor Pool Picks New York Jets Geno Smith and the New York Jets are off to a 2-4 start, but they’ve been competent so far this season. Not only are the Jets 4-1-1 against the spread, but they rank sixth in the NFL in opponent yards per play and are 10th in EPA/Play on defense. The offense isn’t nearly as good (19th in EPA/Play, 22nd in yards per play), but the Jets have a very favorable matchup against a winless Miami Dolphins team – at home – in Week 7. Miami is coming off a bye, but it has just one game all season where it’s scored more than 13 points. The Dolphins rank 28th in EPA/Play, 27th in success rate and 22nd in yards per play allowed through five games this season. While I don’t believe either one of these squads is a playoff team, the Jets have a much higher floor with Geno Smith under center. New York has also hung around with playoff contenders like Green Bay, Detroit and New England while beating a 4-2 Cleveland team in Week 5. I have no faith in this Miami team, which seems destined for a top-three pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Miami had a backdoor cover against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 5, but it has relied on garbage time to get back into games that never were really close to begin with. With De’Von Achane out for the season, Malik Willis doesn’t have enough help to really get this offense going, and now he has to take on a Jets unit that has been one of the better ones in the NFL. Since the Texans are the only big favorite on the board this week – and they're just 2-4 themselves in 2026 – I don’t mind taking a shot on the Jets. I can’t imagine another spot (outside of their road game vs. Miami) where I’d really feel comfortable taking them in Survivor. – Peter Dewey Minnesota Vikings Despite the Minnesota Vikings being undefeated so far this season, this might be the last week I'd feel confident taking them. They're fresh off a bye week and have arguably the best defense in the NFL. That very same defense is going to be able to put Daniel Jones and the Indianapolis Colts' offense in a blender. It's clear by now that the key to beating the Colts is stopping Jonathan Taylor, and the Vikings rank in the top three in virtually every single run defense stat. Kyler Murray should be able to produce enough offense to let his defense lead them to a win in this interconference duel. – Iain MacMillan Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. picks.blurb: 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7 Cole Smith, Vikings Wire Thu, October 22, 2026 at 3:55 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings enter their Week 7 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts looking to extend the league's longest winning streak. Since Week 14 of the 2025 season, the Vikings have won 10 straight games, building a 5-0 record going into last week's bye. They face a 2-4 Indianapolis team that fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday, one day after losing 26-20 to the previously winless Tennessee Titans. Head coach Shane Steichen is still employed , but the Colts feel combustible right now, with rumors of trading away star players like RB Jonathan Taylor and G Quenton Nelson swirling. Minnesota can't afford to overlook Indianapolis if they want to keep pace with the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers. But this feels like an opportunity for the Vikings to jump on an inferior team that is going through organizational changes. Here are three bold predictions for the Vikings when they host the Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday. Jordan Mason will run for 100+ yards and 2 touchdowns Jordan Mason appears to return to the lineup after missing the past four games with a thumb injury that landed him on injured reserve. Kevin O'Connell told Paul Allen on Tuesday that he expects to see Mason, Jordan Addison, T.J. Hockenson, and Christian Darrisaw back at practice on Wednesday . With Mason back, Minnesota can return to its 1-2 punch with Aaron Jones. Indianapolis enters Week 7 as one of the league's worst run defenses. They rank 22nd in rushing yards allowed, but their 4.8 yards per run allowed is tied for 5th-worst in the league. Their 12.3% stuff-rate ranks 30th in the league, and they rank last in EPA/run allowed. I expect the Vikings to stay committed to the run game and give Jones some relief after he carried the ball 85 times for 370 yards from Weeks 2 to 5. Mason averaged 3.5 yards after contact per carry in 2025, tied for 11th-best in the league among qualifying running backs. I see him breaking 100 yards and reaching the end zone twice on Sunday. Jauan Jennings will catch a touchdown pass Trade rumors swirled around Jauan Jennings in the days after Minnesota's 23-13 win over the Saints in Week 5. He was caught on camera slamming his fist into the ground following Myles Price's fumble that was returned for a touchdown. That came two plays after Jennings appeared to get open for a potential touchdown, but Murray instead threw an incompletion to Tai Felton. One play later, Murray slightly overthrew Jennings in the end zone. Jennings has caught only two passes for nine yards this season, but the rumors of a potential trade seem to have died down. He's gotten open enough that he should be getting more targets, but look for him to find more separation downfield, with Justin Jefferson, Addison, and Hockenson potentially back this week. With extra attention on the other weapons on the field, Murray will make up for his red zone misses against the Saints. The Vikings will sack Daniel Jones 5+ times and pick him off multiple times This will be the first time Daniel Jones plays against the Vikings since spending the end of the 2024 season with them. He signed with the Colts last year and played well until a fractured fibula in Week 12 slowed him down, and an Achilles tear ended his season two weeks later. He completed 68% of his passes for 3,101 yards (8.1 yards per attempt), 19 touchdowns, and eight interceptions. Jones hasn't been as efficient this season, completing 59.6% of his passes and averaging 5.9 yards per attempt, with four touchdowns and six picks. He has been pressured on 42.1% of his dropbacks, tied for the league's 7th-highest mark. Of course, no one pressures quarterbacks as much as Minnesota does. They have a league-high 47.8% quarterback pressure rate, spearheaded by a 67.0% blitz rate that is 24.5 percentage points higher than the next-closest team. Look for the Vikings to get after Jones all day and force him into turnovers. This article originally appeared on Vikings Wire: 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7

But across six decades of Minnesota Vikings football, one cross-conference foe in particular has acted less like a casual visitor and more like an ultimate inflection point: the Colts. Before Minnesota hosts Indianapolis at noon (CT) Sunday, a look back at the franchise vault reveals an undeniable trend: When the Vikings play the Colts, trajectory shifts follow. In 1969, after the Vikings dropped a one-point contest at the Giants (while facing their former and, later, future quarterback Fran Tarkenton) in the season opener, Minnesota returned home to battle the (Baltimore) Colts. The Vikings scored 52 points — tied for the second-most in a game in franchise history — and the 38-point victory ignited a 12-game win streak that remains the second-longest in franchise history (regular-season games only). Minnesota went on to win the NFL Championship that season before falling in Super Bowl IV to Kansas City. Fast forward to 2022, when Indianapolis — in its fifth game under Jeff Saturday as interim head coach after the Colts fired Frank Reich midseason — traveled to Minneapolis to take on the Vikings in Week 15. After failing to clinch the NFC North title the week prior in Detroit, Minnesota dug itself into a massive 33-0 halftime deficit. The Vikings continued fighting, however, outscoring the Colts 36-3 in the second half to force overtime. In OT, Greg Joseph connected on a game-winning 40-yard field goal, helping the Vikings not only win 39-36 and secure the division, but also complete the largest comeback in NFL history. Then, just two seasons ago in 2024, the Vikings started the year with a 5-0 record. Following a Week 6 bye and back-to-back losses against the Lions and at the Rams, Minnesota hosted Indianapolis looking to get back on track. The Vikings went on to defeat the Colts 21-13 on Sunday Night Football , sparking a nine-game win streak. As Kevin O'Connell's squad welcomes Indianapolis (and former quarterback Daniel Jones) to U.S. Bank Stadium, the Vikings will try to win their 11 th consecutive contest. Indianapolis won't get much going other than Jonathan Taylor again this week. 5 of 5 experts pick the Vikings, NFL.com Analysis from NFL.com's Bobby Kownack: The last time the Colts made a big midseason change, firing Head Coach Frank Reich and replacing him with former player Jeff Saturday in 2022, they defeated the Raiders in their very next game. Will history repeat itself on Sunday after the Colts fired General Manager Chris Ballard following their loss to the previously winless Titans? No. No, it will not. The Vikings have too formidable a defense, and the Colts have too many shortcomings on both sides of the ball, for that to happen. Minnesota is stout against both the run (fifth in yards allowed) and pass (third), increasing the probability that Daniel Jones encounters big problems should Brian Flores' defense slow down Jonathan Taylor. The Colts QB has done little this year to show he's the same guy who appeared to have revived his career with Indy before tearing his Achilles last season. Also, Kyler Murray looked sharp in the Vikings last outing, throwing for 229 yards and a touchdown with an 80 percent completion rate. Assuming Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Prior to its two recent victories over the Colts, Minnesota had dropped six consecutive games against Indianapolis from 2000-20. Battling the Bye Since the 1990 season (when the bye week was officially implemented into the schedule), the Vikings are 22-15 all-time in games immediately following a bye, including a 12-5 mark at home. From 1990 to 2009, Minnesota was dominant in post-bye contests, going 17-4 (the Vikings had two bye weeks during the 1993 season). During the past two decades, however, the bye hasn't been kind to Minnesota; the Vikings have won just five times in such games (2015 against Kansas City, 2017 at Washington, 2020 at Green Bay, 2022 against Arizona, and 2023 at Las Vegas) and have lost the past two games right after the break.
