away.headline: Colts' Week 6 injury report gives fans every reason to expect a Titans win
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts must feel pretty good about their health because they released Darius Slayton even though the team has struggled with wide receiver injuries this season. Not so much in Week 6, even though Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is going to be out and Alec Pierce still is . The positive is that Indy has a bye week, also known as having a matchup against the Tennessee Titans. As for Alec Pierce, no timeline exists for when he might return after reinjuring his heel. That might not happen until midseason, and the Colts will probably have far tougher games than the Titans before Pierce comes back. Besides Dulin, the only Indy player who will miss the game, according to head coach Shane Steichen , is linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs), but both Carlies and Dulin missed Week 5, and the reason the team lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers had nothing to do with the absences of Dulin and Carlies. The reason was that the defense was terrible again. Therein lies the difference between the Steelers and the Titans, as no matter how bad Indy's defense can be at times, Tennessee doesn't have the offensive talent that Pittsburgh has. Indianapolis Colts should be healthy enough to easily defeat the Tennessee Titans in Week 6 The Titans are 31st in the NFL in yards per play (4.5), last in points scored (58), 28th in quarterback rating (77.2), and 27th in rushing yards per game (82.6). Unless Indianapolis was without defensive lineman DeForest Buckner, cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, and most other good starters, Indianapolis should be able to outscore Tennessee easily. And Buckner, Ward, and Gardner are healthy and will play in Week 6. The Titans haven't beaten Indianapolis since October 2022, a stretch of six straight wins for the Colts, and Indy has no excuse for not making that seven straight victories at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday. Injuries won't be a problem for the Colts, at least heading into the game. Tennessee won't have starting safety Kevin Winston Jr., but otherwise they are mostly healthy. They just don't have a lot of talent. They haven't defeated any AFC South team since January 2024, and if that changes against the Colts in Week 6, Indianapolis needs to make some immediate changes. Ultimately, Sunday should be a get-healthy game for the Indianapolis Colts as far as record and standing in the division. When all else is going on, at least Indianapolis can count on two wins every season against the dismal Tennessee Titans . home.blurb: Defensive lineman Jalen Redmond was one player the hosts singled out as an example of the pursuit required for that plan. The Vikings need that kind of response across the defense if Jones is able to avoid the initial rush. One part of the podcast’s original setup has changed from a certainty into an injury question. Colts tight end Tyler Warren (groin) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday, but he remains listed first on the Colts’ Week 7 unofficial depth chart and had not received a game designation in the latest report. Warren’s availability matters because Indianapolis can use him as a blocker, receiver and screen-game piece. If he cannot play or is limited, Minnesota has one fewer versatile Colts option to account for. The Minnesota Vikings have a chance to make Sunday’s home game against the Indianapolis Colts a test of patience for Daniel Jones. The Colts quarterback has experience in Minnesota from his brief 2024 stop with the club, but the Vikings’ defense under defensive coordinator Brian Flores presents a different kind of pressure problem: force short throws, rally to the football and make Indianapolis repeatedly execute. Locked On Vikings After Dark co-hosts Luke Braun and Arif Hasan focused their Colts preview on that formula. In their review of True Media data, they said Jones had the NFL’s third-lowest average depth of target on plays when a blitz was picked up and did not produce pressure. Their point was not simply that Minnesota needs sacks. It was that Flores can use pressure looks to invite checkdowns, then trust the defense to limit the yards after the catch. Flores has made the blitz central to his approach, but Braun and Hasan noted that Minnesota also uses plenty of zone and two-high coverage. That matters against an Indianapolis offense they viewed as less effective against zone looks and two-high shells. If Jones immediately moves the ball to the flat, the Vikings have to turn those throws into modest gains instead of allowing easy drives to develop. The Vikings host the Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 25. home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Colts, they had some players upgraded and one added- linebacker CJ Allen. picks.blurb: Four Bold Predictions for Dolphins-Jets - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview Four Bold Predictions for Dolphins-Jets Mark H. Stowers Sat, October 17, 2026 at 5:47 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Miami's Oct. 25 visit to MetLife Stadium matches two limited offenses and two teams trying to define their seasons. The Jets are early 4.5-point favorites, but the Dolphins' improving rushing attack creates room for several bold predictions. Ollie Gordon II will rush for at least 100 yards. Gordon has totaled 188 yards in two starts since De'Von Achane went on injured reserve. Miami's 217-yard performance against Cincinnati should convince the coaching staff to keep the offense on the ground. New York has been much stronger against the pass than the run, which gives Gordon a favorable path to volume. Malik Willis will produce two touchdowns and no more than one turnover. This is the prediction that would change the game. Willis threw two interceptions and lost a fumble against Cincinnati, but the bye gives Miami time to reduce his difficult reads. Designed runs and play-action can turn his mobility into production while limiting risky throws. Miami will record at least three sacks. The Dolphins have only four sacks through five games, making this the boldest defensive call. Hafley's staff has two weeks to design pressure packages against Geno Smith. A healthier edge rotation and more aggressive use of linebackers could finally create the disruption missing against Cincinnati. The game will be decided by three points or fewer. The early total sits below 40 at several books. New York averages 18.6 points and Miami 14. The Jets have the stronger defense, while the Dolphins have the more productive recent running game. Neither team has shown enough passing explosiveness to create confidence in a runaway. A reasonable projection is Jets 20, Dolphins 17, but that margin leaves the upset door open. If Miami wins the turnover battle, Gordon controls the tempo and special teams avoid another disastrous start, the Dolphins can reverse the score. Bold predictions are not promises. They are matchup-based possibilities. The first three require Miami to emerge from the bye with a more disciplined offense and a more creative defense. If those changes appear, the fourth prediction should follow naturally.

Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton Doubtful the Miami Dolphins (0-5) climb out of the cellar in the AFC East this season, but if they are going to, it almost has to begin with a win Sunday afternoon at MetLife Stadium against the New York Jets (2-4). For New York, Sunday offers an opportunity to take another step big picture as an organization and in the moment remain on the fringe of the playoff picture. The Jets are certainly far more competitive than they were a season ago but after a loss last weekend to the Patriots and looking at the rest of their schedule, a win Sunday at home against the winless Dolphins is paramount. They will need more from their offense, though, if they are to win as the Jets average just 18.7 points per game. Miami’s offense is scoring an average of 14 points per game but it’s worse than that for the winless Dolphins. Miami has yet to even lead for even a second in any of their five games this season. New York enters the game following a 26-19 loss to the Patriots in Week 6. The Jets fell behind early and could not overcome their mistakes despite another competitive defensive effort. Prior to that defeat, they snapped a four-game losing streak with a 17-12 win over Cleveland, showing the formula they hope to replicate against Miami: strong defense, ball control, and avoiding turnovers. The Dolphins’ most recent outing was a 31-24 loss to Cincinnati on October 11, arguably their most encouraging offensive performance of the season. Miami rallied in the second half and scored 24 points after managing only 46 total points across its previous four games, but defensive breakdowns once again proved costly as the losing streak extended to five games. Quarterback play will be one of the game’s biggest storylines. Veteran Geno Smith has provided stability for the Jets, throwing for 1,336 yards with seven touchdowns and just one interception through six games. While the Jets’ offense has not consistently produced explosive numbers, Smith has protected the football and given New York a chance to win most weeks. Not the same situation in South Beach. Miami’s Malik Willis has been underwhelming. Yes, the skill positions are lacking with the Dolphins, but the long-time Green Bay backup has to be better. Willis has thrown for 849 yards with a mere two touchdowns along with four interceptions. The Dolphins need greater efficiency if they are going to win or even lead a game. The Dolphins swept both meetings in 2025, including a 34-10 victory at MetLife Stadium last December. away.blurb: Both players were listed as limited participants, and there's absolutely no guarantee that either will be ready to go for the Week 7 game against the New York Jets. "He was a big bright spot early on," Hafley said. "Everybody was excited about him from training camp to preseason and the first couple games that he played. We were counting on him and then unfortunately he got injured. Monday he was out there, limited. Today he'll be out there and getting acclimated again. My expectations can't be too high because we've got to see him practice today. We've got to see how he feels tomorrow, kind of like Kyle. And then Friday to see what he's able to do and if he's able to go and help us out. But I am excited. I'm very excited. We've got two young players practicing that we're excited about, and we'll see what they can do today." The bottom line here is that having Douglas and Louis back will help when they're able to return, but maybe it won't happen this week, and if it does, maybe we shouldn't expect too much too soon from either of them. MIAMI GARDENS ― Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis was treated for an injured thumb on his right, throwing hand, but he fully practiced four days before a Week 7 game at the New York Jets . Willis did not throw at a bye week Monday practice that was open to reporters. Willis did not mention the thumb injury when he met with reporters a short time before the first Jets injury report of the week was released. "(Coach Jeff Hafley) just wanted to get us a little rest, and he wanted to get some young guys in there and see how they were progressing through this season," Willis said when asked what he was dealing with. "But, pretty good." Hafley said at the start of the week that Willis would be fine. "He should be good," Hafley said. "I mean, was he dealing with something? Yeah, I mean, we had a bunch of guys after the (Cincinnati) game that were having a Tuesday practice; usually we don't go until Wednesday. So just rested him on that, but I foresee him being good to go." Miami Dolphins injury report includes Malik Willis thumb Willis has said he hasn't been good enough in his first five Dolphins starts. He is 29th in the NFL with a passer rating of 68.4. He has 2 passing touchdowns, 2 rushing touchdowns, 4 interceptions and 5 fumbles. Willis said he balanced football review and rest and recovery during the bye week. What does Willis think about outside of football? "I mean, the Lord, bro," Willis said. "I keep waking up every day. I got an opportunity to come in here and do my job. I have a family that loves me. I have more than enough. I make it to work safe every day, bro. It's a dangerous world. And we just overlook all these things that are blessings. I try not to do that. And at the same time, I hold myself to the highest of standards. And I just try to focus on the process. home.headline: Dolphins-Jets Injury Update: Bye Leaves Key Miami Questions Open
home.blurb: Miami's Week 6 bye prevents the Dolphins from issuing a conventional Friday game-status report, so no player should be labeled officially out or questionable for the Oct. 25 Jets game unless the club has made that designation. The week still produced several important health developments. Right guard Jonah Savaiinaea did not participate in Tuesday's voluntary practice after leaving the Cincinnati game with an ankle injury. Linebacker Jordyn Brooks, edge rusher Robert Beal Jr., cornerback Reese Taylor, running back Jaylen Wright and receiver Caleb Douglas also sat out. Because it was a bye-week session, some absences may have been precautionary. The Jets' Friday report belongs to their Week 6 game, not the Miami matchup. Breece Hall, guard Dylan Parham, receiver Adonai Mitchell and edge rusher Joseph Ossai were listed out after missing practice with injuries. Safety Dane Belton and tight end Kenyon Sadiq carried questions, while Omar Cooper Jr. entered a return window from injured reserve. Whatever happens in New York's game this weekend will become the starting point for its Miami report. The matchup implications are significant. If Savaiinaea cannot return, Jarrett Kingston is the likely replacement against a Jets defense with 17 sacks. If Brents, Taylor or Duck remain unavailable, Miami will again ask young defensive backs to cover Garrett Wilson. If Hall's quadriceps injury lingers, Braelon Allen would become New York's primary runner. away.blurb: Three Pittsburgh Steelers have been ruled out for the team's Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, and five more are questionable to suit up, according to the team's Friday injury report. Two wide receivers Ben Skowronek and Roman Wilson left the team's 34-22 Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts with injures and did not return — and they won't be back this week, either. Skowronek suffered a calf injury early in the second quarter, and then Wilson injured his left hand on the final offensive drive of the first half. Wilson had a large wrap on his left hand after the game. On Monday, head coach Mike McCarthy said neither player will return to active this week. Fellow wide receiver DK Metcalf was initially listed as questionable to play after missing practice on Friday with an illness, but he has now been cleared to play. Tight end Pat Freiermuth is also questionable to play after suffering a calf injury in practice on Saturday. Strong safety DeShon Elliott remains limited in practice and will not return this week. Starting cornerback Jamel Dean was ruled out last week, but might be ahead of the curve on the initial multi-week estimate for his injury. He is listed as questionable. Running back Rico Dowdle , who is recovering from a dislocated toe on his left foot, is also questionable to make his return to the lineup, as is defensive tackle Keeanu Benton , who has an ankle injury, and defensive who has an ankle injury, and defensive back Jalen Ramsey , who has played through his broken wrist the last two weeks. A beat up Steelers defensive kept Tom Brady out of the end zone for 55 minutes and Mitch Trubisky successfully replaced an injury Kenny Pickett as Pittsburgh beat the Buccaneers, 20-18 at Acrisure Stadium on Oct. 16, 2022. Pickett threw his first career touchdown pass to Najee Harris in the first quarter, but a hit from blitzing linebacker Devin White knocked him out of the game. Chris Boswell kicked two field goals and Trubisky found Chase Claypool for a six-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter to extend the Steelers lead. With 4:45 to play, Brady finally punched through a defense that was playing without T.J. Watt , Minkah Fitzpatrick , Ahkello Witherspoon , Levi Wallace and Cam Sutton with a touchdown pass to Leonard Fournette, but Devin Bush broke up the two-point conversion attempt, and Trubisky and the Pittsburgh offense ran out the clock. Defensive run game coordinator and outside linebackers coach Larry Foote had two stints with the Steelers, playing from 2002-08 and 2010-13 after the team made him a fifth-round draft pick out of Michigan. Foote was a two-time Super Bowl champion in Pittsburgh and also won a Super Bowl LV ring as a coach with Tampa in 2021. home.headline: Jaelan Phillips is out, but his injury isn’t the only puzzle Panthers have to solve
home.blurb: Canales soon clarified that Phillips will be out for Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers: “I know there are advantages to game plans, but this is something that we need to address and take care of.” With Phillips officially out — it’s unclear if he’ll be ready by the Panthers’ Thursday Night Football game against the Packers in Week 8 — the Panthers are missing more than a run-of-the-mill defensive starter. The 27-year-old who the Panthers signed to a four-year, $120 million contract this free agency has lived up to his billing as a premier pass rusher; he has 2.5 sacks through five games but has also added 18 total pressures in the pass rush — 24th among all edge rushers , according to Pro Football Focus. Phillips has also been stout against the run and a vocal leader his teammates praise. What’s also a result of Phillips being out? The absence of Phillips comes at the same time as reserve outside linebacker and special teams ace Thomas Incoom is also “week to week” with a calf injury. Incoom exited the Eagles in the first half and didn’t return, and as a result the Panthers needed to do a whole bunch of roster magic to fill his role on special teams. In each of the four special teams units Incoom contributes on — kick return, kick coverage, punt return, punt coverage — the Panthers needed to replace him with four different players, Canales said. Canales was asked if the Panthers will elevate anyone from the practice squad with Phillips and Incoom out, and he indicated that Nick Hampton would. The interior offensive lineman was placed on the team’s injured reserve before the season began due to a hamstring injury and is now waiting for his 21-day practice window to be activated. When asked Wednesday, Canales was vague about Christensen’s situation: “We’re just evaluating it, and you gotta figure out roster spots as well,” before adding that he has faith in the team’s current slate of IOLs. If Christensen were to return, that limits their flexibility to use the injured reserve. It’s also worth noting the Panthers have already waived someone off the injured reserve with an injury settlement — Claudin Cherelus a few weeks ago — to avoid further limitations. It’s possible, perhaps likely, that once Cherelus gets healthy, he’d re-sign with the Panthers, rejoining the squad without forcing the team to use one of its eight precious IR-elevation moves. home.headline: Injuries threw Panthers rookie CB Will Lee III into deep end. Now, he's just 'trying to eat'
home.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles put that moniker to the test Sunday, when Lee often matched up against DeVonta Smith, a 2021 top-10 pick and Heisman Trophy winner out of Alabama. Though Smith caught a touchdown against Lee in the fourth quarter of Carolina's 25-14 win, the 2026 fourth-round pick finished with six tackles and three pass breakups, becoming the first Carolina rookie with three passes defensed in a game since Keith Taylor in 2021. "It was a great matchup. He's a great receiver, Heisman winner, wide receiver one over there in Philly. And he's a great guy to compete against," Lee said. "That's my big thing. I love competing. I don't care who it is out there, I'm gonna go out there and give it my all." "Talk about Will Lee and the way that he was challenging their best receiver or whoever they put out in front. He got some penalties called on him, but he was in the mix, and he was right there at the top of coverage," Canales said. "He could be a little cleaner with his hands, but I'm not going to back Will Lee off of playing that style of football. I thought that was excellent." The 6-1, 195-pound Lee was known for his strong man coverage skills at Kansas State, where he played in 2023, and Texas A&M, where he spent his final two college seasons. He developed a reputation for being physical and handsy at both stops, not unlike the scouting report on Horn after the Panthers drafted him with the No. 8 pick out of South Carolina in 2021. "I'm a juco guy. I'm grimy. I like to play physical. It's all love at the end of the day, but I'm a competitive person," he said. "I feel like you're out there to embarrass me, and I'm out there to stop you from doing what you're supposed to do. I'm trying to eat, so that's my goal." "He said it's just like repetition. You've gotta learn and feel out the game when you're out there. Some refs are gonna call it different than others, and you've just gotta play the game," Lee said. "He just said be confident in yourself out there and your technique, and you're gonna be just fine." "His demeanor is that of a veteran," Scott said. "A lot of times when you're out there as a young guy, you might have to keep them from being up and down with the result of the drive or the play, giving up a big catch or getting a PBU. They kind of ride that wave. But Will, for the most part, is pretty steady, which definitely makes it easier on everybody." Injuries threw Panthers rookie CB Will Lee III into deep end. home.blurb: On the bright side for the Bucs, it appears that starting quarterback Baker Mayfield has a chance to return in Week 7. Mayfield, who dislocated his thumb in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings, appears to be nearing a return to practice, as NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported ahead of Week 6 that there is "optimism" that the former No. 1 overall pick will return against the Carolina Panthers. Pelissero: There's "optimism" that Baker Mayfield (thumb) will return Week 7. While that move could be a reaction to Sunday's results after Carolina picked up a win against Philadelphia, it's also possible that oddsmakers aren't quite sold on the Bucs getting their starting quarterback to return just yet. Ravens HC Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson did get in some “limited” work today. https://t.co/3rq60qmJVB The Ravens opened as three-point favorites at home in this massive Week 7 matchup against AFC North foe, and that line bounced around from 2.5 to 3 in the lead up to Wednesday's practice. However, Jackson was not spotted at the beginning of practice and was later seen walking off with a limp. As a result, oddsmakers at DraftKings quickly shifted the odds in this game to Bengals -1.5, a huge 4.5-point flip from where they were entering the week. Lamar Jackson (ankle) seen walking off practice field with a limp, per @CordellWoodland . https://t.co/1R708hsFHo That's a sign that Jackson isn't expected to play in Week 7, and he may need to log a full practice on Thursday or Friday to shift the sentiment in the betting market. Sports Illustrated spoke to multiple oddsmakers this week about how they set the line for a game like this with Jackson's status up in the air. "Your lookahead line, you essentially have to assume he's going to play until you hear otherwise.," Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook, told Sports Illustrated. "So, that's baked into the price, whether we anticipate he'll be at full strength or 80% strength, that would kind of be factored in there. "And then, as the week goes on, we'll adjust as we know more. Obviously, he wasn't at practice today, and our line went down a point and a half just off that alone. And then we'll kind of trickle down as the week goes on and his status becomes more and more certain one way or the other. If he's back at practice tomorrow in a limited or full capacity, the line will probably shift back towards the Ravens. If he's not there again on Thursday, we'll essentially start pricing as though [Tyler] Huntley is going to be the starter." So, what could the line close at if Huntley makes his third start in a row? "If he's out and it's Huntley again, the line will most likely shift to the Bengals being the favorite, probably in that 1.5 to 2.5 range," Gour said. So, based on Gour's projection, the current line suggest that Jackson won't play. That would be a huge blow to a Ravens team that is 4-2 and already lost a division game in Week 6. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score while leading the NFL in yards per attempt, yards per completion and passer rating. The Ravens are 7-12 all time without Jackson, though they've won three of the four starts Huntley has made in his place since the 2025 season. As for the Baltimore Ravens , their kicker is on notice. These teams meet in a Week 7 AFC North clash, and here are bold predictions for the contest. The Bengals (3-2) enter the game in last place in the division despite having a winning record. That's because the Ravens, Steelers, and surprising Browns all have a record of 4-2. It should be another battle for the Ravens and Bengals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joe Burrow will riddle the Ravens' defense for 3 TD passes When the Bengals are right, they are tough on offense. And they've been cooking this year, ranking No. 9 in the NFL in points per game. Burrow is connecting on 71.4% of his passes. He has 11 touchdown passes and three interceptions. Look for him to keep the momentum going this week. But Burrow needs to take care of the football, which Zac Taylor said would go a long way in helping the Bengals win, according to Cleveland.com. "The turnovers is what screams at you," Taylor said. "That leads into field position." And Taylor said Burrow and his teammates are ready for this matchup. "It's exciting," Taylor said. "I think our guys really get fired up for this game. Not that they don't get fired up for every game, but whenever we play in Baltimore in a road divisional game, it's a fun one to get up for, and our guys will be up for it." Bengals RB Chase Brown will score two TDs One of them will be on the receiving end of a pass from Burrow. Brown will have a nice day, despite being caught in a time share with Samaje Perine, according to The Athletic. "I think we'll continually assess how that touch share between (Perine) and Chase Brown should play out," Bengals offensive coordinator Pitcher told Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. "Every game's different. What type of scheme we lean into is going to factor into that. Obviously, what we ran more of yesterday leans into what Samaje does well, which is get downhill and run through contact." The Bengals haven't forgotten about their ground game. "You strive for balance when it comes to run-pass," Pitcher said. "You're always wanting to be the most balanced and versatile version of yourselves. It's like those are high-level goals that you set out to attain. But never in any given situation are we going to let a high-level theoretical goal get in the way of what it means on Sunday to win a game and what is the feedback we're getting in a game on a given Sunday." Derrick Henry will rush for 80-plus yards and a TD Henry is still smarting from last week's fumble that led to the Ravens' loss to the Browns. He took blame for the game-changing turnover , according to ESPN. "I got to take care of the ball," he said. "There's no excuses for that. I got to be better. I put the team in harm's way. I sound like a broken record with this, but I got to go back to work on it. Can't put the team in that situation." Teammate Kyle Hamilton took up for Henry. "Obviously, he's Derrick Henry, Hall of Fame running back [who] wants to hold onto the ball," Hamilton said. "He knows that. He's his harshest critic, so I'm not going to say anything ill about it. He's put us in position to win a lot of games." All of this will motivate Henry for a big game against the Bengals Ravens WR Ja'Kobi Lane will catch 5 passes and score a TD Lane looked ready to roll against the Browns in his return from injury. And he should be able to carve out a significant role in Week 7. Lane looked great in training camp. The injury short-circuited his 2026 season. But now he's back in the mix. His overall stat line could be impacted if Tyler Huntley is still at quarterback. But if Jackson is back, this could be a breakout game for Lane. Who will win the game? The Bengals should be able to outscore the Ravens in this matchup. But the key factor is Jackson. If he's back, the Ravens have a much better chance of winning. But we will still roll with Burrow, Chase, and Tee Higgins having a big game, along with Brown doing his thing. away.headline: Ravens list 15 players on Wednesday injury report ahead of Bengals
away.blurb: Lamar Jackson was listed as limited Wednesday with an ankle injury, while Cam Jurgens was a full participant as he continued working toward his Baltimore debut. Outside linebacker Tavius Robinson did not participate because of a pectoral injury. Jackson's designation was the biggest update after he missed the opening portion of practice available to reporters. Coach Jesse Minter later said Jackson got limited work, and the official report confirmed his participation. Rashod Bateman was listed as limited with a shoulder injury after exiting Sunday's loss to Cleveland. Bateman has 16 receptions for 233 yards and a touchdown, with 11 catches producing first downs. Rookie tight end Matthew Hibner also was listed as limited with a hand injury. Hibner has five catches for 70 yards and a touchdown. Cornerback T.J. Tampa, designated for return from injured reserve, was listed as limited with rest, toe, and ankle designations. He recorded 29 tackles, two passes defensed and an interception last season. Calais Campbell joined Robinson as the only nonparticipants, receiving a rest day. Mark Andrews and Trey Hendrickson practiced fully despite hand and finger injuries, respectively. Baltimore listed 15 players overall. Thursday's practice will provide the next indication of whether Wednesday's progress carries into the remainder of Bengals week. Tampa remains on injured reserve and has been designated for return. Jackson has missed two consecutive games after leaving the Tennessee matchup at halftime on Oct. 4. In four appearances, he has completed 68 of 96 passes for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception, posting a 119.6 passer rating. He also has 144 rushing yards and a touchdown on 19 carries. Jurgens practiced without a red non-contact jersey and was listed as a full participant with a concussion. Full participation is encouraging, though it does not independently confirm completion of concussion protocol or availability against Cincinnati. Before the trade from Philadelphia, Jurgens played 242 offensive snaps this season, including 187 at left guard and 55 at center. Pro Football Focus charged him with 12 pressures allowed, including one sack, across 146 pass-blocking snaps. away.headline: Bengals Injury Report: Solid Cincinnati Health Continues as Attention Focuses on Lamar Jackson
away.blurb: Meanwhile, Baltimore star Lamar Jackson (ankle) went limited again on Thursday after practicing Wednesday for the first time since suffering the injury in Week 4. “Lamar [Jackson] was actually able to get a little bit of limited work in today in preparation. So, that’s where that’s at. Again, it’s a day-by-day thing, but he was able to get a little bit of work in and be involved in the preparation," Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said about Jackson on Wednesday before commenting on the specific workload. "[I am] not really [going] to get into the specifics of anything with that. I know this, when it’s ready for [Lamar Jackson] to be able to play, from both sides, and we feel like that’s the best thing to do; that’s what we’ll do.” Check out the full injury report below as Cincinnati tries to capitalize on its pretty great health coming out of the bye week: Bengals Injury Report: Solid Cincinnati Health Continues as Attention Focuses on Lamar Jackson Skip to main content SI.COM The Bengals injury report stayed pretty clean on Thursday. Cincinnati is battling Baltimore on the road at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday and even had their lone player upgrade on the injury status line. Kyle Dugger (quad) went full in Thursday's practice. No other Bengals popped up on the injury report . His status is a bit murky, but he did a lot more at practice today and now seems like near-lock to play in the contest. The Ravens should definitely have newly added center Cam Jurgens on the field after he recovered from a concussion. He practiced fully on Wednesday and Thursday. Ravens fans are hoping he's snapping to Jackson and not Tyler Huntley on Sunday. Minter sounded very confident Jurgens will play. Most of the other notable injured names like Mark Andrews (hand) and Calais Campbell (rest) are dealing with minor problems or just rested on Wednesday. A lot of Ravens upgraded to full showings in practice. “Yes, Cam [Jurgens]’s doing great," Minter noted. "I think the weekend was really good for him to get past the protocol, and also allow him a lot of time to really, really pick up on things and study. So, again, he’s done a really good job. He’s a veteran. He’s played in a couple of different offensive systems now, which I think I mentioned a while back. [The Eagles] had a system there. Then they learned a new one this year. So, I think he’ll really be in tune and ready to be able to help us this week.” Published 14 hours ago RUSSELL HELTMAN Russ Heltman is on the Bearcats and Bengals beat for On SI. Cincinnati signed S Russ Yeast from the practice squad to the active roster, giving the Bengals five at the position to work with, but their No. 3 option should be good to go. Defensive tackles Jonathan Allen and B.J. Hill each had rest days Thursday, with Allen missing all of practice and Hill missing part of it. Most of the Ravens listed above are on track to play Sunday, like wide receiver Rashod Bateman (shoulder), guard Ioane Vega (ankle), and left tackle Ronnie Stanley (toe/ankle), all of whom went full after being limited Wednesday. Safety Jaylin Hawkins (knee) did not practice at all Thursday after he was listed as limited Wednesday, so he may trending toward not playing. EDGE Tavius Robinson (pectoral) was a DNP again. Quarterback Lamar Jackson (ankle) went limited again, and if he goes full Friday, it will be very likely he plays Sunday for the first time since Week 4. The Cincinnati Bengals received a major update Wednesday as they prepare for Sunday's AFC North showdown with the Baltimore Ravens . Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson was not present at the start of Wednesday's practice, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Jamison Hensley. Hensley reported that backup quarterbacks Tyler Huntley and Joe Fagnano were warming up without Jackson. The two-time NFL MVP has not played since suffering an ankle injury against the Tennessee Titans on October 4. His availability for Sunday's matchup against Cincinnati remains in question. For the Bengals, the difference between facing Jackson and Huntley could be significant. Baltimore has already played two games without its star quarterback. And with an important divisional matchup approaching, Jackson's absence Wednesday provides another reason to monitor his recovery closely. There were additional developments concerning Jackson's status later Wednesday. Meanwhile, Alex Glaze reported that Jackson was spotted leaving the practice field without appearing to have participated. Glaze also noted that Jackson was walking with a limp. While Minter's comments confirm that Jackson was able to participate in some capacity, his status for Sunday's game against Cincinnati remains uncertain. Jackson's absence comes just two days after Ravens head coach Jesse Minter suggested Wednesday could provide more clarity about the quarterback's status. Minter continued to describe Jackson as day-to-day during his Monday press conference . When asked whether Jackson might practice this week, Minter responded, "Potentially." However, the quarterback was not among the players warming up during the portion of Wednesday's practice observed by reporters. Now, at the beginning of Week 7, there is still concerns surrounding Jackson's status. home.headline: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson inches one step closer toward injury return
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens are sure hoping superstar quarterback Lamar Jackson can return after he missed the past two games with an ankle injury. Jackson returned to practice in limited form on Wednesday, and there were still plenty of questions about whether or not he could go against the Cincinnati Bengals. On Thursday, the Ravens released another injury report, and Jackson was listed as "limited" for the second straight day, which bodes well with regard to his chances of playing against the Ravens' AFC North foe. Jackson reportedly "moved around well" during the practice session that was open to the media. Jackson suffered the injury in Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans, and Tyler "Snoop" Huntley has been filling in under center for Baltimore. Huntley led the Ravens to a 30-23 overtime win in Week 5 against the Atlanta Falcons, and he threw for two touchdowns while rushing for another. In Week 6, the Ravens fell to the Cleveland Browns, 13-10, on the road, and Huntley went just 19-of-31 for 165 yards with a score. The Ravens are 4-2 and the Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers are also 4-2. The Bengals are 3-2, so the AFC North is very crowded with one-third of the season in the rearview mirror. Jackson has a chance to play on Sunday, and his final status should be revealed this weekend. Want more articles like this? Follow Yardbarker on MSN to see more of our exclusive NFL content. And the pieces could certainly be in place for the Texans to make that third consecutive win become a reality. Their offense is looking the best it has all season after another strong performance from C.J. Stroud. The defense will have the task of facing a new starting quarterback on the other side in J.J. McCarthy , and all of that coming back on Houston's home field tends to make their chances look even better. And when looking at the Texans' betting odds heading into Week 7, it's becoming pretty clear that the sportsbooks have one obvious favorite in mind for this weekend's action in Houston. Texans Already Projected to Rout the Giants in Week 7 According to recent odds from FanDuel Sportsbook , the Texans are now listed as 10.5-point favorites (-550 ML) over the Giants in Week 7. That's by far the Texans' highest spread heading into any week they've played this season. And when looking around the league's Week 7 matchups, Houston is currently the only team listed as a favorite by more than a touchdown––let alone being a favorite by double digits. Stroud (7) celebrates his touchdown with wide receiver Nico Collins (12) against the Tennessee Titans during the second half at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The projected point-total for these two teams doesn't look favorable for the Giants either. Houston and New York have an over-under sitting at 43.5, which comes in tied for bottom-five among the NFL in terms of projected totals for Week 7. The projected point-total for these two teams doesn't look favorable for the Giants either. Houston and New York have an over-under sitting at 43.5, which comes in tied for bottom-five among the NFL in terms of projected totals for Week 7. So if the Texans are projected to win by double-digits, and the total score isn't expected to reach above 43 points, that's not much of an optimistic statement from the books on how this Giants offense could fare against a Houston defensive unit that many considered among the best in the NFL heading into this season. Will the Texans Actually Dominate the Giants as Expected? Now, projections are one thing. Clearly, the consensus is starting to lean in one clear direction for this one between the Texans and the Giants. But does Houston actually have what it takes to make that double-digit victory come to fruition? Really, it all relies upon the defense. Last game against the Jacksonville Jaguars showed that the Texans' offense is starting to get into a bit of a rhythm . A ton of receivers are getting involved and making plays, the run game showed signs of life against one of the best rushing defenses in the NFL, and the offensive line even held up to zero sacks. But the Texans' defense just hasn't been as consistently elite as this team proved to be last year. That's not saying they can't find their way back to that level–– because the personnel looks virtually identical to last year outside of a select few changes. But we still need to see Houston have multiple strong weeks defensively to really have this level of confidence in their chances on Sunday. After all, the Giants have won three games as is this season. That's more than the Texans can claim for themselves, and New York sits atop the NFC East because of it. So as 10.5-point underdogs, they seem just a slight bit underrated here, simply when considering Houston's inconsistencies on defense. Maybe the Texans wind up crushing those projections anyways, but perhaps the Giants can make this game just a little bit more interesting than the odds tend to show. Going to venerated Wembley Stadium, facing off against the division-leading Jaguars, who had the advantage of having played in England the week prior and didn't have to worry about their body clocks, and managing to get away with a win was huge for the Texans. Houston, now at 2-4 but having won two straight road games against division rivals, returns to NRG Stadium to host the New York Giants of New Jersey. The Giants, sitting at 3-2-1, come into this matchup atop the NFC East, despite not winning in their last two games, a tie at Washington and a loss against New Orleans. In their last game, they fell to the Saints 34-27, but the Saints held a lead of 34-10 at one point in the 4th Quarter. Likely because of that QB uncertainty, along with Houston's recent winning streak and the supposed talent disparity, the opening odds from FanDuel for the upcoming matchup between the Texans and the Giants are strongly supporting Houston at home: Overall, this may seem a bit high of an opening line. The Giants haven't played as difficult a schedule as Houston and they are coming in with key injuries and roster concerns. However, the Texans, even coming off a huge win against Jacksonville, are still struggling on defense and sit at 0-3 at home. They have only beaten the Giants once in 6 total meetings, and that was in 2002. Sandwiched between an international game and a bye week, this has the feel of a trap game for Houston. This particular line may tighten a bit as the week progresses, especially as the Giants sort out their QB situation and both teams sort out their respective injury situations. picks.headline: NFL predictions, Week 7: Not much faith in Giants to upset Texans
picks.blurb: NFL predictions, Week 7: Not much faith in Giants to upset Texans | Big Blue View Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A New York Giants Community Big Blue View October 23, 2026 Big Blue View Notifications Notifications Get The iOS App Sections News By/For Fans The Feed Community Guidelines Today's Trivia Betting Betting News FanDuel NFL Odds FanDuel Super Bowl Odds New York Giants Odds NFL Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search Get The iOS App Sections Expand News By/For Fans Expand The Feed Betting Expand Betting News All communities Notifications New York Giants odds BBV staff picks for NFL Week 7. How does the Big Blue View staff see Sunday’s New York Giants vs. Houston Texans game? See our picks for that game and the rest of the NFL Week 7 slate below. Bottom line up front: I don’t expect the Giants to win this game. I won’t go so far as to say that they can’t win the game, but things are stacking up against them. The Giants are, frankly, beat up. left tackle Andrew Thomas is dealing with his groin injury, right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor has his calf injury, and offensive tackle Marcus Mbow suffered a knee injury at the end of the Saints game. Cornerback Greg Newsome II, safety Jevon Holland, and cornerback Colton Hood are in the concussion protocol, and tight end Theo Johnson is still dealing with a neck injury. On the flip side, DeMeco Ryans has retaken control of the Texans’ defense, while C.J. Stroud has been playing some of the best football of his career. And though the Texans’ run game has been bad, Stroud is getting weapons in WRs Marvin Harrison Jr. and Tank Dell, while the Giants are scraping the bottom of the depth chart in their secondary. Starting J.J. McCarthy could provide a spark to the Giants’ offense and allow them to play the style of football for which they were built. But I just don’t know if that would be enough in the face of the Giants’ injuries. A win going into the BYE week would be an amazing boost and allow the Giants to keep pace in the division. And the upset could absolutely happen — football has been weird this year and we’ve seen some absolutely wild outcomes. But I’m afraid this could be an ugly one for New York. Tony Del Genio I’ve thought since before the season started that this was one of the most likely games for the Giants to lose. The Texans’ poor start made me start to reconsider. Their defense, one of the best in the NFL last year, has had a slow start. Cornerbacks Derek Stingley Jr. and Kamari Lassiter have not played up to their previous standards, so there is an opportunity for the Giants to stay in the game and pull off an upset if they can get their passing game to click. The Texans have given up more than 30 points three times. Last week Trevor Lawrence shredded them for 306 yards and 4 TDs. Alas, the strength of the Texans’ D is their pass rush off the edge, with the NFL’s best pass rusher, Will Anderson Jr., and Danielle Hunter (14 sacks and 60 pressures between them) leading the way. The Giants sadly have Andrew Thomas and Jermaine Eluemunor both dealing with injuries. If both cannot play or play at less than 100%, it may be a long afternoon for J.J. McCarthy in his first Giants start. Despite my misgivings about John Harbaugh making him the starter in this game rather than after the break, McCarthy does give them the best chance to mitigate the Texans’ pass rush. The Texans’ run defense is not formidable, but to say the least the Giants’ run blocking is not either, regardless of who the lead running back du jour is on Sunday. When Houston is on offense, C.J. Stroud got off to a bad start this season but has played much better for the past month. The Giants’ defensive back room is decimated by injury, with Greg Newsome, Jevon Holland, and Colton Hood all dealing with concussions, although Paulson Adebo is expected to be back this week. Who is going to cover Nico Collins, one of the NFL’s best big receivers, is anyone’s guess. Jaylin Noel and Xavier Hutchinson are no slouches, either, and the Giants will see Marvin Harrison Jr. for the second time after he caught his only TD of the season again them in the Arizona game. Pick : Texans David Hartman The Giants head to Houston this Sunday after a disappointing home loss to the Saints. J.J. McCarthy came out of the bullpen in the second half of that contest and the Big Blue news of the week is that McCarthy will start this game. The timing is slightly surprising given that New York has its Bye next week, but here we are, with a former Top-10 pick getting a shot at reviving his career after he failed in Minnesota. Can J.J. lead his team to victory, and keep the G-Men in first place in the division? This writer is very skeptical, although to be fair the Giants will remain in first place through Week 7 regardless of the outcome of this game. Weird, right? The plight of the once-mighty NFC East is a story for another day. Houston has some of the best defensive personnel in the NFL, led by edge Will Anderson, Jr. and corner Derek Stingley, Jr. In last year’s AFC playoffs, C.J. Stroud was a turnover machine and an absolute mess, but Demeco Ryans’s defense was suffocating and almost carried the Texans to the AFC Championship game. This season has been an inexplicable reverse, with Stroud playing out of his mind and the defense giving up a ton of yards and points, especially through the air. The Texans started 0-4 but have won their last two, including a huge win in London last week over the first place Jaguars. Don’t expect a letdown, as they’re still reeling from their horrible start, and need this game badly. McCarthy’s play last week was encouraging, but it was in mop-up duty against a bad defense that pulled some of its starters. This is a real test, and it’s hard to ignore the 2025 tape of J.J. He was that bad (hence, his fifth round price tag when New York traded for him). His mobility is a plus, and Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely have been uncoverable recently. Still, I don’t see McCarthy avoiding mistakes and playing well for 60 minutes, or the Giants pulling off the upset. Houston is a very good team, despite its losing record. Valentine’s View Whether I picked them to win or not, with the exception of the Week 2 game against the Los Angeles Rams, I have felt that the Giants have had a good opportunity to win each game thus far this season. I can’t say I feel good about their chances. I am not sure why the point spread has ballooned from 7.5 points to start the week to 10.5 as of Thursday, but I know I don’t have confidence in the Giants’ ability to upset the Texans. The Giants squandered real opportunities to win games the last two weeks, coming away with a tie and a loss in games they easily could have won. That stretch may haunt them. What I fear most, honestly, is the Texans’ defense. Houston has been middling on defense so far, but allowed the second-fewest points in the NFL last season. There is a breakout game coming. With the Giants switching quarterbacks, struggling to run the ball, and entering the game with their top three offensive tackles at less than 100%, I think that might be this week. I don’t want it to be, but I think J.J. McCarthy’s debut as the starting quarterback might turn ugly. away.headline: Philadelphia Eagles sign ex-New York Giants OL Evan Neal
away.blurb: The Alabama product was taken seventh overall by the Giants in 2022 and went on to appear in 29 games with 27 starts, all of them at right tackle. Injuries and recurring struggles in pass protection limited his production over those seasons. Head coach John Harbaugh gave Neal a clean slate this offseason on a one-year deal, only for the team to release him during final roster cuts in August. After a brief stop on the Las Vegas Raiders' practice squad, Neal worked out for the Eagles on Wednesday, practiced with the team Thursday, and was officially added as a guard. Philadelphia Eagles sign ex-New York Giants OL Evan Neal - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Philadelphia Eagles sign ex-New York Giants OL Evan Neal Dan Benton, Giants Wire Fri, October 23, 2026 at 12:55 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Former New York Giants offensive lineman Evan Neal has landed with the Philadelphia Eagles , who signed the 2022 first-round pick to their practice squad on Thursday. New York moved Neal inside to guard ahead of 2025, but he never took an offensive snap and spent time on injured reserve (IR). The move provides Philadelphia additional depth amid ongoing offensive-line concerns. From the Giants' perspective, Neal's arrival in Philadelphia closes another chapter on a high draft investment that never developed into the long-term starter the franchise once expected. New York has continued to reshape its offensive line without him as he searches for a foothold elsewhere. away.headline: Giants Injury Report: Giants O-line Thinned By Injuries
away.blurb: Thomas, who has sat out Wednesday and Thursday over the past several weeks and returned to practice on a limited basis on Friday and Saturday before being cleared to play, is someone to watch this week. Last week he came out of the game just before the big fourth-quarter comeback attempt against the Saints; the veteran left tackle was visibly laboring through his groin injury throughout the game. Starting safety Jevon Holland was spotted at practice, off to the side with a trainer. Newsome and Holland have been the Giants defensive secondary’s best players so far this season, so hopefully their absences aren’t serious enough to keep them out of Sunday’s game. Speaking of the cornerback position, Newsome did not practice, but rookie Colton Hood (concussion) did. Sills, 6-foot-6 and 325 pounds, was originally an undrafted free agent out of Oklahoma State whom the Eagles signed in 2022. That season, Sills, who has played guard in his short NFL career, was one of three undrafted free agents to make the Eagles roster but only appeared in one game for Philadelphia. Giants Injury Report: Giants O-line Thinned By Injuries Skip to main content SI.COM The New York Giants will face one of the best defenses on Sunday when they travel to Houston to meet the Texans. So it was a bit alarming that on Wednesday, the team’s top three offensive tackles were not practicing. Starters Andrew Thomas (groin), Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and swing tackle Marcus Mbow (knee) were not participating in practice during the media viewing period. Eluemunor missed last week’s game as well with his injury after saying he would test it to see if he could anchor; he is also someone to watch this week. And with MBow now nursing something, the Giants could be thin at offensive tackle if he can’t play. The Texans have league sack leader Will Anderson, Jr. on one side of their formation and Danielle Hunter on the other. That would be quite the test for rookie J.C. Davis, who would presumably play left tackle; at right tackle, the Giants could potentially move Sisi Mauigoa from right guard to tackle, the position he played in college. Edmunds, Newsome Not Spotted During Media Viewing Portion of Practice Inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) and cornerback Greg Newsome II (concussion) were not spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. If Edmunds can’t go, Micah McFadden would get the start. The question then becomes who would wear the radio in his helmet: rookie Arvell Reese, the most likely candidate, or someone else. Rookie Colton Hood (concussion), receiver Darnell Mooney (neck), safety Tyler Nubin (neck), and tight end Theo Johnson (neck) were spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. Paulson Adebo’s Practice Window Opens Cornerback Paulson Adebo’s 21-day practice window is now open. If he clears, he could fill the roster vacancy left after Tuesday’s release of running back Najee Harris and defensive lineman Jihad Ward. Adebo has been on IR since Week 2

away.headline: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out?
away.blurb: The Giants ruled out safety Tyler Nubin (neck), tight end Theo Johnson (neck), and cornerback Colton Hood (concussion). WR Chris Olave (illness) didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but he was able to work on a limited basis during Friday's practice. He should play so long as that illness is behind him. DL Nathan Shepherd (illness) also missed two days of practice with an illness that's been going around the locker room. He was limited on Friday as well. CB Lorenzo Styles Jr. (knee) was limited on both Thursday and Friday, so don't be surprised if he's a game-time decision. RB Alvin Kamara (back) practiced on limited reps throughout the week. The Saints didn't bring up either of the two running b acks on their practice squad so it does llook like he'll play. Starting offensive linemen Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) are both questionable for the Giants, as is edge rusher Abdul Carter (calf). There's a crowd of Giants players available to play after being listed on the injury report this week: cornerback Greg Newsome II (groin), outside linebacker Malik Harrison (groin), defensive back Elijah Campbell (thumb), running back Najee Harris (ribs), tight end Isaiah Likely (foot), wide receivers Darnell Mooney (neck) and Charlie Jones (Achilles), as well as safety Jason Pinnock (concussion). As was the case last week, the following Saints players are on injured reserve with season-ending injuries: defensive tackle Bryan Bresee, running back Ty Chandler, cornerback David Long Jr., tight end Moliki Matavao, offensive lineman Dillon Radunz, and cornerback Rejzohn Wright. However, a couple of others have been designated to return after sitting out at least four games: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and veteran running back Travis Etienne Jr. are both expected to return after the bye week in November but it sounds like we won't see left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. until December at the soonest. Offensive lineman Nick Saldiveri is on the season-ending PUP list (physically unable to perform), while wide receiver Mason Tipton is eligible to return after missing four games. Tipton has not returned to practice yet. LS Zach Wood (calf) returned from injured reserve and is expected to play. The Saints don't have another long snapper on the roster. home.blurb: Tank Dell was a full participant in Houston's first official Week 7 practice as he prepares for his long-awaited return Sunday against the New York Giants. But seven Texans did not practice Wednesday because of injuries, including Azeez Al-Shaair, Reed Blankenship, Trent Brown, Blake Fisher, David Montgomery, Jalen Pitre and Dalton Schultz. Head coach DeMeco Ryans already confirmed earlier this week that Dell will play against New York. Wednesday's full participation is another encouraging step toward making that return a reality. Dell has been designated for return from injured reserve, and Houston has spent the past several weeks gradually increasing his practice work. Pitre did not practice because of his shoulder injury, while Blankenship was sidelined with concussion and hand issues. This is not the week to allow protection problems to return, since the Texans have a bye week following. Houston might need another big afternoon from that young secondary on Sunday. The interesting wrinkle is who will be throwing against it. New York coach John Harbaugh confirmed Wednesday that J.J. McCarthy will start against Houston. That should immediately put pressure on Houston's pass rush to make McCarthy uncomfortable. home.blurb: Azeez Al-Shaair has made strides in his recovery and is nearing a return to the field ahead of the Houston Texans ' Week 7 matchup this weekend. This presents concern for New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy, who will be the starter against Houston. Al-Shaair played in the team's first five games of the 2026 campaign. However, he suffered a minor knee injury against the Jacksonville Jaguars as he is on the team's injury report. He was absent from Houston's practice session on Wednesday before improving to limited activity during Thursday's session. It indicates that the injury might not prevent him from missing out on Week 7. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ian St. Clair Wed, October 21, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos are coming off a huge win over the defending Super Bowl champs. Next on the docket is a scrappy Arizona Cardinals bunch that just pulled a huge road upset of the Los Angeles Rams. The good news for the Broncos (4-2) is that they got the mini-bye week before heading to the desert and could get a few players back from injury and the commissioner's exempt list. Denver looks to extend its winning streak to three games after coming out of a gauntlet to start the season. The Broncos are currently -4.5-point road favorites over Arizona (2-4). The total sits at over/under 43.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -115. Offensive Rankings Denver : Thirty-first in total offense (252.2 yards per game), 26th in rushing offense (84.2 YPG), 28th in passing offense (168.0 YPG), 26th in scoring offense (19.0 points per game). Arizona : Twenty-third in total offense (307.3 yards per game), 22nd in rushing offense (96.3 YPG), 20th in passing offense (211.0 YPG), 24th in scoring offense (21.0 points per game). Defensive Rankings Denver : Twenty-second in total defense (348.3 yards per game), 31st in rushing defense (139.8 YPG), 10th in passing defense (208.5 YPG), tied for 10th in scoring defense (20.8 points per game). Arizona : Twenty-third in total defense (350.5 yards per game), 20th in rushing defense (120.8 YPG), 22nd in passing defense (229.7 YPG), tied for 31st in scoring defense (29.7 points per game). Here are the MHR staff's keys to Sunday's game. Win the line of scrimmage on offense The Broncos offensive line has been the definition of "meh" to start the regular season. It's nowhere near what it's been the last few seasons, but it also isn't horrid either. Denver needs to dominate the line of scrimmage on Sunday. Open lanes in the running game and do a better job of pass protection. It's a cliche, but success on offense starts in the trenches. Getting that could lay the foundation for jump-starting the offense. — Ian St. Clair Bench Bo Nix; Start Jarrett Stidham Just kidding. Ya'll crazy if you think benching Bo Nix is even remotely the answer. That said, Bo Nix does need to play better, and he isn't seeing the field well to start the season. He's had slow starts in every season he's played, so, for now, I'm chalking this up to another slow start. However, seven games in, I'm hoping to see him take flight a bit now that the hardest part of the Broncos' schedule is complete. At 4-2, they got through it with a winning record, and that is all we could hope for. — Tim Lynch Pressure the QB The key to this game is the same as it has been every week. Get to the QB. The defense has done a great job this season of causing mayhem in the backfield. Make it uncomfortable for Jacoby Brissett (like the back of a Volkswagen). When QBs are harassed and hurried, they make mistakes. — Adam Malnati Disciplined, execution-based offensive football This team needs to execute at a high level, and it will win this game easily. The defense is already there. If the offense can up its game, this Broncos team will be unstoppable. — Sadaraine Limit the impact of Trey McBride The Broncos defense has performed well this season, aside from a few games. For the most part, they've been able to limit the impact of the opposing team's top player on their offense. This week, they face All-Pro tight end Trey McBride, who is coming off a sensational 2025 season. He is the focal point of Arizona's aerial attack and gets over ten targets per game. Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph needs to come up with a good game plan that limits his impact on the game. If they can slow him down, Denver will have a great shot at earning their fifth victory of the season. — Christopher Hart What are your keys to Sunday's game?

away.headline: Broncos Week 7 Injury Report: RB Tyler Badie Trending Toward Inactive
away.source: Denver Broncos On SI on MSN
away.blurb: Coleman was designated to return from injured reserve on Wednesday after missing the last four games. He still must be formally activated to the 53-man roster but is fully expected to play against the Cardinals. Coleman's return is especially helpful this week considering third-string RB Tyler Badie missed practice for a second straight day due to a thumb injury. His status for Sunday's game is in jeopardy; he needs a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up. Outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) both also were DNPs this week. Hufanga will be ruled out on Friday, and the Broncos anticipate Elliss landing on short-term injured reserve, back at some point later this year. “He’s going to be someone that it’s not season-ending, and so we’re fortunate. So that’ll come out later in the week, but it was better news," head coach Sean Payton said of Elliss on Wednesday. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) and cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) were limited participants; Surtain could be a game-time decision, though Waddle is expected to go. Arizona listed starting safety Budda Baker and running back Jeremiyah Love as DNP for a second consecutive day, as well as safety Andrew Wingard. Cornerback Garrett Williams and defensive lineman Darius Robinson were upgraded to limited. “They give you a couple different looks," Payton noted Wednesday. "They’re in their base defense. They have a penny package. You have to I.D. if they’re in that. Then their pressure package from nickel. They affect the quarterback. I think the other thing that stands out is they’re causing more fumbles in their wins. Their takeaway numbers have been really good, and that’s something you see.” Broncos Get Massive Boost with Return of RB Jonah Coleman Broncos' IR Watch: Who's Eligible to Return and What They Bring The Denver Broncos continued full-scale preparation for Sunday's road game against the Arizona Cardinals, releasing their second injury report ahead of the Week 7 matchup. On it, running back Jonah Coleman (ankle) and cornerback Riley Moss (ribs) were listed as full practice participants for another day, while defensive end Zach Allen was upgraded to full after getting his usual rest day on Wednesday. Cardinals Might Be Down Some Starpower Unfortunately for the home team, the Cardinals are trending toward being at much less than full strength -- at least, according to their Thursday injury report . Baker's absence in particular would be a fortuitous break for a Broncos offense desperately seekin its first true breakout game in 2026. However, Payton knows well enough not to overlook the other 10 players on the Cardinals' defensive side. away.headline: Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return
away.blurb: Running back Jonah Coleman, who has been designated to return from IR with his ankle injury, practiced in full on Wednesday. Patrick Surtain II, who left the team's Week 4 game with an ankle injury, was also at practice on a limited basis: Unfortunately, Tyler Badie, Talanoa Hufanga, and Jonah Elliss all did not practice, and Elliss' injury could end up being more extended. Hufanga hurt his ankle in Week 5 against the Los Angeles Chargers, and both Badie and Elliss got hurt in Week 6 against the Seattle Seahawks. Fortunately, Hufanga's injury is minor. As for Surtain, James Palmer is reporting that the likely return for the Defensive Player of the Year is Week 8 against Kansas City, but he also didn't totally shut the door on Surtain playing this week : Him practicing in limited fashion does give him a chance to play, but you almost want to wonder if the Broncos understand the opponents they have coming up and want to ease Surtain back into things for Week 8, as that game could carry major impact across the division and conference in terms of seeding. All in all, the Broncos seem to be trending toward being more 'full strength' for the Chiefs game in Week 8. However, not only could Coleman find his way back into the lineup in Week 7, but, until he's ruled out, Surtain could be nearing a return as well. The Broncos also have wide receiver Pat Bryant on IR. He is eligible to return f in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Denver plays Arizona, Kansas City, and Carolina before the Week 10 bye, which just so happens to line up nicely with the trade deadline. This article was originally published on predominantlyorange.com as Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return . The Denver Broncos have dealt with their share of injuries this year, unfortunately. The bright side though, is that the Broncos are consistently among the least-injured teams in the NFL, and the ailments this year have largely been minor. As the middle of the season approaches, the playoff race will slowly start to heat up, and Week 8 against the Kansas City Chiefs could present a legitimate playoff atmosphere. Before the Chiefs, though, the Broncos have to get by the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. And in the team's first injury report of the week, it does seem to indicate that the team could get some key players back. With Love expected to remain sidelined, Arizona could once again turn to Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to handle the rushing responsibilities. The Cardinals leaned on their running back depth during last week’s victory, but facing Denver presents another challenge for an offense attempting to establish consistency. The Cardinals have invested heavily in the rookie’s long-term future, and his availability will be an important storyline as the season progresses. Jahdae Barron and Taylor Rapp have done a nice job stepping up in the secondary while PS2 and Hufanga have been sidelined. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET New England Patriots (+3) at Chicago Bears Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime This is a big game for both teams, a tough one for the road team on a short week. Both teams can score, which should make this a fun one to watch. I think the Patriots have the better defense and that will be the difference. They overcome the road to win a much-needed game. Pick: Patriots 28, Bears 27 Pittsburgh Steelers at New Orleans Saints (+3.5) Paris on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) These two are both coming off road victories and now have a long trip to play this one. The Steelers have been the more consistent team this year, but the Saints looked good last week against the Giants . This will be tight, but the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 27, Saints 26 San Francisco 49ers at Atlanta Falcons (+3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The 49ers are rolling as the league's best team, especially on offense. But losing Mike Evans will hurt. The Falcons couldn't stop the Bears last week, so what's to think they will slow down Brock Purdy ? They might not. But the Falcons will keep up. It's close. Pick: 49ers 30, Falcons 28 Cleveland Browns at Tennessee Titans (+1.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Browns are 4-2 after beating Baltimore last week, while the Titans beat the Colts last week. Neither team is doing much on offense, which suggests this will be a low-scoring game. I think the Browns have a better defense, which will be the difference. They win it again on a late field goal. Pick: Browns 17, Titans 16 Indianapolis Colts (+6.5) at Minnesota Vikings The Vikings are off a bye, while the Colts are off a terrible home loss to the Titans. That led to the firing of general manager Chris Ballard. Maybe that gives the Colts a bump. Beating the Vikings' defense will mean a lot of Jonathan Taylor . I think we see that as the Colts keep it close, but just miss out on the upset. The Denver offense has been lifeless so far this season. But the defense is still sticky. I think that defense will come up big, while Bo Nix finally makes some plays. It's close. They are playing much better on both sides of the ball. The two defenses will be challenged here, but the Lions will be the better offense at home coming off the bye. Lions win it by a tiny margin as both quarterbacks light it up. Pick: Lions 34, Packers 33 Los Angeles Rams at Las Vegas Raiders (+4.5) This is a must-win for both teams, as they are on losing streaks. The Rams have a lot of injury issues, which have really impacted their team. They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here. But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders , who hang around. And let's not forget the Chiefs have Patrick Mahomes . Seattle is good on defense, but their offense is turning the ball over. That matters here. Chiefs take it. picks.blurb: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Green Bay Packers in Week 7 Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI On Sunday afternoon, the Detroit Lions will take on a red-hot Green Bay Packers team that has won three straight games. Most recently, the Matt LaFleur-led squad dispatched of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, 23-13. It marked the third consecutive game in which Green Bay held its opponent to 14 or fewer points. And on the season, the Packers’ defense – coordinated by former Arizona Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon – has allowed the 10th-fewest points in the NFL (20.8/game). Meanwhile, on the opposite side of the ball, Green Bay – led under center by sixth-year passer Jordan Love – has scored the 10th-fewest points in the game (21.2/game). Through six weeks, Love has also completed just 59.7 percent of his pass attempts. If the season ended today, it'd rank as his lowest completion percentage as a starting quarterback in the NFL. Yet, multiple Green Bay pass-catchers have flourished, most notably wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson, now in his fifth NFL season, has already amassed as many touchdowns as last season (six) and nearly as many receptions (29) and reception yards as he did a year ago (538). The former second-round pick secured 35 catches and 611 yards in 10 games a season ago. Meanwhile, Golden, Green Bay's first-round pick in 2025, has already surpassed all his receiving totals from his rookie campaign. He's already racked up 30 catches, 501 yards and three touchdowns amid a career breakout season. And just like Watson, he's well on pace for a 1,000-yard receiving campaign. Consequently, both Watson and Golden possess the potential to wreak havoc against the Lions’ secondary, even with Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch back in the fold for Detroit. In addition to Watson and Golden, the Lions will also likely have their hands full with Packers running back Josh Jacobs. The Pro Bowler returns to the lineup after spending the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner exempt list for an offseason domestic abuse incident. Jacobs, who's coming off a 929-yard, 13-touchdown rushing campaign in 2025, should provide an immediate boost to Green Bay's league-worst ground game. In case you were wondering, the Packers have compiled a measly 359 total rushing yards through the season's first six games. Expect Jacobs, along with Watson and Golden, to give Kelvin Sheppard's defense its fair share of fits on Sunday. However, at this present juncture, I'm still willing to give the Lions a 60 percent chance to pull off the Week 7 victory at home. Pick: Bears -3 (-102) Steelers vs. Saints The Saints have the worst run defense in the NFL, and now they have to take on a strong Pittsburgh run game. Pick: Steelers -3.5 (-102) 49ers vs. Falcons The Falcons' secondary is banged up, and now they have to take on an MVP candidate in Brock Purdy. San Francisco's offense should be able to score at will in this game. Pick: 49ers -3 (-102) Browns vs. Titans The Browns are just a better version of the Titans. Pick: Vikings -6.5 (-108) Dolphins vs. Jets The Dolphins have had one of the most difficult schedules in the NFL to begin this season. This is by far their easiest opponent yet, so maybe the Dolphins will be able to put up a fight.
