On the other side of the image is Lions QB Jared Goff with RB Jahmyr Gibbs and a logo for the Detroit Lions behind them. Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:21 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFC North still looks like one of the NFL's most competitive divisions just six weeks into the 2026 season. Every team in the division finished with a winning record in 2025, and that trend has continued into this year . Now the Packers and Lions are gearing up for a huge divisional matchup that could have huge ramifications come playoff time. Green Bay is looking strong after a questionable start to the season. They are on a three-game winning streak after taking care of Dallas on Sunday Night Football . The Packers are still a bit behind the Vikings, but getting a win in Week 7 will get them one step closer to catching up. Meanwhile, Detroit quieted their doubters in Week 5 after crushing Arizona in the desert. The Lions even got a solid game from their defense, something that has eluded them for most of the season. But Detroit is coming off their bye week, so it is impossible to know if they'll carry over that momentum or come out flat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Which team will come out on top in this massive divisional matchup? Here are three bold predictions before the NFC North clash between the Lions and Packers in Week 7. Jared Goff throws his first interception of the season, but still shreds Packers defense Mark Konezny-Imagn Images Goff may be the most underrated quarterback in the entire NFL this season. He may look like a quarterback from a different age, but Goff can still sling it with the best of them. Detroit's franchise quarterback has 1,485 passing yards with 12 touchdowns and zero interceptions through five games. That's right, he still has not thrown an interception at any point this season. This speaks to how careful Goff is with the football, no doubt owing to his veteran experience. All of that said, this could be the week that the streak comes to an end. The Lions should not underestimate the Packers' defensive unit, even if they don't have Micah Parsons in Week 7. Green Bay has one of the better coverage units in the NFL this season despite an unproven cornerback room. Even more impressive is that they lead the NFL in interceptions with nine through the first six games. If any team is going to snap Goff's streak, it will be the packers. Goff will throw his first interception of the season against Green Bay on Sunday. All good things must come to an end, including his impressive streak of clean games. However, that doesn't mean he'll wilt against the Packers. Detroit will finish this game with at least 400 passing yards, shredding Green Bay's secondary from wire to wire. Josh Jacobs rumbles for 100 rushing yards, two touchdowns in 2026 debut Green Bay's one weakness this season has been their rushing attack. The Packers are averaging a pitiful 59.8 rushing yards per game this season. That is due to a combination of offensive line issues and a thin running back group. But the latter is about to change. Josh Jacobs looks slated to return in Week 7 after being removed from the commissioner's exempt list. "I would say Jacobs has been preliminarily cleared and is expected to play this week. He is going to practice. He's going to be on the field. They say he has kept in good shape, and the Green Bay Packers, who have had a really solid start to the season, probably could use a little bit of an improved running game, and they get Josh Jacobs in Week 7 to come in and do it," NFL insider Ian Rapoport said on Wednesday via Good Morning Football. Getting Jacobs back won't fix everything overnight. After all, it is fair to be skeptical of how ready he truly is after staying away from football for over a month. Still, Jacobs could have a breakout game against Detroit if Matt LaFleur dials up enough carries for him. Jacobs will go over 100 rushing yards and score two touchdowns against the Lions. Green Bay wins an NFC North shootout thanks to Detroit's compromised defense Mandatory Credit: Wm. Glasheen USAToday Network via IMAGN images Of course, the matchup that everyone will be watching in this one is Jordan Love against Detroit's struggling secondary. Green Bay suddenly looks capable of keeping up with Detroit's offense. The emergence of both Christian Watson and Matthew Golden has unlocked the team's passing attack. On paper, they're in the same tier as Detroit in terms of passing yards per game. The good news for the Lions is that Brian Branch is expected to make his 2026 debut against the Packers in Week 7. It is impossible to know just how good Branch will look after last season's Achilles injury . Getting him back is also no guarantee that Detroit's defense will magically play better. But it is a start. In the long term, getting Branch back should do wonders for the Lions. Unfortunately, it won't be enough to win this game. The Packers win by one score in an epic shootout at Ford Field. Related: Caleb Williams and Drake Maye are on fire. Can either defense make a stand in Bears-Patriots? picks.headline: Lions vs. Packers preview: 3 key matchups
picks.blurb: Lions vs. Packers preview: 3 key matchups - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview Lions vs. Packers preview: 3 key matchups Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard reacts to a play against Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half at Ford Field in Detroit on Monday, Oct. 20, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Anthony Balaj Fri, October 23, 2026 at 10:30 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Detroit Lions (3-2) will have an opportunity to reestablish themselves in the NFC North in both Week 7 and Week 8 as the Green Bay Packers (4-2) and the Minnesota Vikings (5-0) travel to Ford Field. This is not a situation most Lions fans are very familiar with. In my lifetime, the storyline with these types of divisional games was whether the Lions could finally establish themselves as true division contenders. But never to reestablish as one. Just take the 2025 NFC North standings in for a moment. Look at them again. I've seen the Lions at the bottom far too often in my 34 years. After getting the taste of what it was like at the top in 2023 and 2024, it felt like last place would never be the case again as long as Dan Campbell was leading the Lions. Unfortunately, it happened. Oh, and look. It could happen again because this division is the best in football. It's not slowing down. The race is on. Brian Flores and the Vikings defense is not waiting for the Lions young offensive line to gel before it comes to Detroit. Ben Johnson and the Chicago Bears are not waiting for the Lions young defensive coordinator to find his footing while seeking to repeat as division champs. Matt LaFleur and the Packers are not waiting to the Lions secondary to solve its problems before attacking it with deep shot after deep shot. No, the Lions are at the bottom. Feel it. Breathe it in. Remember the decades at the bottom. In a way, it feels like this is truly the first game of the season. This is how it was always meant to be. Don't get me wrong, the 2023 and 2024 teams are without question the best and most memorable seasons of my Lions fandom. But the story of Dan Campbell's Detroit Lions was always meant to overcome adversity. To get kicked in the teeth. To get knocked down. But before long, they are going to be the last ones standing. Three key matchups. Three opportunity to reestablish . Ford Field vs. Packers' offense Green Bay comes into Ford Field ranking 29th in presnap penalties with 22 on the season . The key matchup here is the Lions fans at Ford Field against the Packers' discipline before the snap. Of course, presnap penalties are drive killer for most any NFL offense. But that is amplified for the Packers who have no running game and are last last in rushing yards per game (59.8), yards per carry (2.9), and rush EPA (-0.299) . Playing behind the sticks making the Packers even more one-dimensional would be extremely valuable for a Lions' secondary that could use all the help it could get, especially with rookie Keith Abney likely to play often at the safety position. In 2025, the Lions were the beneficiary on only 18 false start penalties, tied for 22nd in the NFL. To go with the 5-3 record on the season, Ford Field was hardly the home field advantage that it had been in the years prior. Sunday is an opportunity to reestablish Ford Field as being one of the most difficult environments for opposing teams to play in. Let me just drop this in here one more time. Kelvin Sheppard vs. poison picked The second key matchup was highlighted well by Jeremy Reisman's question to defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard asking how do does he decide on your poison in a matchup that presents both deep and over-the-middle weapons? "That is the coach's job to make sure that we understand the down and distancing, the tendencies and things like that. What have we seen? And obviously each game things change. You prepare. These coaches are good in this league and they self-scout as well." The Green Bay Packers' deep passing attack is a bit of a paper tiger with some interesting situational tendencies , but nevertheless, it must be respected out of the sheer frequency they attempt it. Last week against the Arizona Cardinals, Sheppard rolled out a unique solution by bracket covering both Trey McBride and Michael Wilson . It won't be that simple this week as the Packers have two deep threats in wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, as well as tight end Tucker Kraft. With the return of safety Brian Branch, Sheppard has the flexibility to pick his poison by game script, down-and-distance, and personnel groupings to put the defense in the best position for success. Branch's return to the field is an opportunity for the Lions secondary to reestablish itself, and it could not have come at a more critical time. Cade Mays vs. Jonathan Gannon Lastly, the third key matchup is Lions' center Cade Mays vs. Packers' defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon. Mays is set to make his Detroit Lions debut with his first start of the season. Gannon is in his first season as Green Bay's defensive coordinator and so far he has made some significant adjustments to his normal defensive philosophy. As discussed in "The Athletic Football Show" clip below, Gannon is dialing up blitzes of 6+ rushing defenders at 2-3 times the rate as he had in either Arizona or Philadelphia. It will be critical for Mays and Jared Goff to be on the same page regarding blitz recognition and communication. If successful, it is very likely the Lions offense reaches 30+ points scored against. Consider this Mays' introduction by fire to the blitz-heavy NFC North, wherein all three of the Vikings (1st, 66.7%), Bears (5th, 39.6%), and (Packers (10th, 32.1%) are in the top ten in the NFL in blitz rate, according to Sumer Sports . Mays has the opportunity to reestablish the Lions offensive line as one of the most intelligent and powerful units in the NFL since the retirement of Frank Ragnow. These are the matchups. These are the opportunities for the Lions to reestablish as the class of the NFC North once again.

The new names to appear a few days prior to the team's Week 7 showdown against the Detroit Lions were linebacker Zaire Franklin and EDGE Lukas Van Ness. Franklin, 30, was brought in this offseason after spending his first eight years in the league with the Indianapolis Colts. According to the report , Franklin is dealing with a shin injury, while LVN appeared on the list due to an illness. The team didn't officially practice on Wednesday, Oct. 21, so all of the injuries and designations listed were all estimations . Roughly 24 hours later, the Packers gave the Lions a better idea of who's struggling and who's in a good place to play on Sunday, Oct. 25. Seeing as the Lions only had three players appear on the initial injury report, it's clear these two teams are in vastly different places. Green Bay improved to 1-1 in NFC North play with a dominant win at home against the Chicago Bears, and they may have won back-to-back games at Lambeau Field, but now it's time for them to head to Ford Field to take on the Lions. On the defensive side of things, Franklin and Van Ness are joined by defensive tackles Anthony Campbell (ankle) and Jordon Riley (Achilles) and cornerbacks Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck) and Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring). For Love to see three of his receivers on the report is a bit scary, but there's still a bit of time before Week 7 rolls around for everyone to get healthy.

home.headline: Packers-Lions Wednesday Injury Report: Here’s What Jordan Love Said About Sore Back
home.blurb: The Green Bay Packers’ star quarterback, who has carried the load for most of the team’s 4-2 start, was deemed limited participation on Wednesday, the first day of on-the-field work before Sunday’s NFC North showdown at the Detroit Lions. Only one player, receiver Bo Melton (back), would not have practiced. Nine players were limited, including Love and receivers Matthew Golden (shoulder) and Christian Watson (ankle). The Lions are coming off their bye. Every player on the roster practiced, including safety Brian Branch, who is set to return from last year’s torn Achilles. Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), CB Brandon Cisse (hip), WR Matthew Golden (shoulder), QB Jordan Love (back), DT Jordon Riley (Achilles), CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), WR Christian Watson (ankle), WR Savion Williams (ankle). Riley has been designated to return from injured reserve and is within his 21-day practice windows. Limited participation: CB Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring). Packers-Lions Wednesday Injury Report: Here’s What Jordan Love Said About Sore Back Skip to main content SI.COM GREEN BAY, Wis. – Jordan Love has taken a beating at times this season. For the first time, it’s shown on the injury report. He said “no” when asked if he was concerned that he will not be in the lineup against Detroit. Coming off a Sunday night game and with a Thursday night game looming against the Panthers, coach Matt LaFleur conducted a “jog-through” practice on Wednesday but will put the team in pads for a “really good” practice on Thursday. That was welcome news for Love. After two games of strong pass protection in wins over Tampa Bay and Chicago, it was another painful week for Love in the win over Dallas. “It’s just dealing with a sore back from the game,” he said. “Just some lingering effects from that. One of those things, we’ll just take it day by day but, obviously, it was nice to have a jog-through day, a little bit more mental day, and just recover.” By the official stats, Love and Cleveland’s Deshaun Watson have absorbed a league-high 45 hits through Week 6. He was hit eight times and sacked on three against the Cowboys. “Obviously, just with the back, I don’t know exactly what play it happened on, when it happened,” Love said. “We talk about all the time: You want to, obviously, limit me taking hits in the pocket. That’s something that we’ve talked about, we harp on, and there’s been some better efforts to do better and protect better. I think guys are responding to that. It’s one of those things, yeah, you want to be able to limit as many hits as I take.” Running back Josh Jacobs, who is returning after six weeks on the exempt list, is not on the injury report. “I’ve been actually practicing with my helmet and shoulder pads, so it’s not like it’s overly different,” Jacobs said. “I don’t know where we’re going to be at this week, or if I’m actually going to play or not. picks.blurb: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:41 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There is a big time injury for the Los Angeles Rams . And the Raiders have a major concern as well. These teams meet in Week 7, and here are bold predictions for the NFL contest. It's a crucial game for the Rams, who stand at 2-4 and find themselves a staggering four games behind the front-running 49ers in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Raiders stand at 3-3 in third place in the AFC West. They're unlikely to be a playoff contender, but are trying to build a strong foundation for 2027. Let's take a look at what could happen when these teams battle. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Matthew Stafford will throw for three touchdowns It's hard to gauge what kind of yardage output Stafford will have. Without the injured Davante Adams, the Rams may lean on the ground game a little more. Adams is the team's leading receiver with 480 yards and four touchdowns. Sure, Stafford still has Puka Nacua. And Nacua will get his targets and yardage. But who steps into the No. 2 role? Maybe the Rams will use tight end Tyler Higbee more. Or perhaps Konata Mumpfield or Jordan Whittington will step up and produce. However, despite the receiver situation, the Rams will need to find a way to get the ball into the end zone if the Raiders load up to stop the run in the red zone. So look for Stafford to spread it around and still get his TD passes. Stafford said he understands the situation , according to The Athletic. "I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win," Stafford said. "In some of those guys' instances where they're going to have opportunities to hopefully come back and play for us, make sure that when they come back and play for us, it's meaningful stuff for them." However, some observers think Stafford has finally reached the end of his NFL rope, according to ESPN. "Stafford can't move," Ben Solak wrote. "He was never the most mobile quarterback, but the Rams were willing to use him on boots in the past. In 2024, 16.8% of Stafford's pass attempts were on the run — an above-average number! That fell to 13.9% in 2025 and is down to 9.6% in 2026. Sure, designed rollouts are down — but it isn't just that. "Stafford has zero scrambling passing yards on the season per NFL Next Gen Stats. He has yet to break the pocket and complete a pass on a scramble drill. The last quarterback to log no scramble passing yards through six weeks of a season was 2022 Tom Brady — the final season of a pocket passing titan." But it's not time to write Stafford off. Rams RB Kyren Williams will rush for 90-plus yards The Rams must run the football against the Raiders, a team that struggles to stop the ground game. The Raiders are giving up 134.3 yards per game, which ranks No. 28 in the NFL. Keeping the ball on the ground needs to be a big part of the Rams' game plan. The Rams have thrown 252 passes with 148 rushing attempts. McVay wants those numbers closer together , according to theramswire.com. "Ultimately, what I care about and what we care about is what's the best way is to move the ball and score points," McVay said. "Because of some of the situations that we've been in, those two-minute situations have gotten us a little bit out of balance. No matter how I cut it, it's an excuse. I'd like to be able to have a little bit more balance. And that's reflected by being efficient on early downs and sustaining drives." One thing is for sure, Williams and the Rams haven't lost their belief that this can be a special season. "Man, my confidence is still as high as ever," Williams said. "We know what we've got on our team and in this locker room. We come to practice every single week. That's why we can't lose our focus. We can't lose what matters the most, and that's the work. "It's about having faith. That the work we put in every single week will come to shine." Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty will split carries with Mike Washington Jr. There's no doubt that Jeanty has been a huge disappointment for the Raiders. They picked him No. 6 overall, expecting a franchise-changing player. Instead, Jeanty has a career average of 3.5 yards per carry. And Washington has been turning heads with the coaching staff, according to a post on the Raiders' YouTube page via Athlon Sports. But he needs to be better at pass protection . "He's a rookie, so he had a lot to catch up on," Kubiak said when asked about Washington's role in the passing game. "He's continuing to improve. (And) he's putting the work in. You see the practice come to life in the games. He's not where he wants to be. He's got to keep growing." Jeanty has been a threat in the passing game. Maybe his future is as a third-down back. Washington could supplant him. And the prediction is for that to begin this week. Jeanty has time to bounce back. It's still early in his career. But he simply hasn't been able to show in the NFL what he showed in college. picks.blurb: NFL Week 7 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Chiefs upend Seahawks, Raiders scare Rams Skip to main content NFL NFL Standings NFL Free Agency NFL News by Team More NFL News Our NFL Sites MLB Standings MLB Trades and Transactions MLB Free Agency Baseball Insiders MLB News by Team More MLB News Our MLB Sites Draft Tracker NBA Free Agency NBA Standings NBA News by Team More NBA News Our NBA Sites Anaheim Ducks Boston Bruins Buffalo Sabres Calgary Flames Carolina Hurricanes Chicago Blackhawks Colorado Avalanche Columbus Blue Jackets Detroit Red Wings Edmonton Oilers Florida Panthers Los Angeles Kings Minnesota Wild Montreal Canadiens Nashville Predators New Jersey Devils New York Islanders New York Rangers Ottawa Senators Philadelphia Flyers Pittsburgh Penguins San Jose Sharks Seattle Kraken St. Louis Blues Tampa Bay Lightning Toronto Maple Leafs Vancouver Canucks Vegas Golden Knights Washington Capitals Winnipeg Jets COLLEGE College Football Men's College Basketball Women's College Basketball Men's College Baseball ABOUT Contact Meet the Editorial Team Our Entertainment Sites The Kansas City Chiefs have been as reliable as possible, the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams have not, the Las Vegas Raiders seem like they just won't go away, and it's safe to say the regular season has gotten off to a wild and weird start as we head into NFL Week 7 . Our picks and predictions each week have been indicative of that. Sorry I didn't have the Arizona Cardinals beating the Rams outright or the Tennessee Titans getting their first win of the season. We persevere and keep going with the picks. It's going to be a fun Week 7 in the league, as the NFL has big-time matchups like Cowboys-Eagles (less exciting than it once was), Chiefs-Seahawks, Rams-Raiders, Packers-Lions and even Patriots-Bears on Thursday night. That's enough to set the stage alone, so let's get right into our NFL Week 7 picks with predictions straight-up and against the spread for every game this week. NFL Week 7 predictions: Picks straight-up and ATS for every game Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NFL Week 7 Matchup Straight-Up Pick Patriots vs. Bears (TNF) Steelers vs. Saints (Paris) Buccaneers vs. Panthers Panthers -3.5 49ers vs. Falcons Bengals vs. Ravens Giants vs. Texans Dolphins vs. Jets Browns vs. Titans Colts vs. Vikings Broncos vs. Cardinals Cardinals +4.5 Rams vs. Raiders Packers vs. Lions Chiefs vs. Seahawks Cowboys vs. Eagles 2026 NFL Picks Straight-Up Record: 58-35 (Last week 7-7) | ATS Record: 43-48-2 (Last week 6-8) Note: All lines are courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 7 prediction to make Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Frankly, there were a lot of tough predictions to make, but taking the Chiefs to go on the road to Seattle and hand the Seahawks another loss outright feels like the one I struggled with the most. With all due respect to the 12th Man and the impact that could have on this game, there's a lot to be worried about when it comes to the Seahawks right now. Sam Darnold and this offense are in dire straits, particularly with their inability to effectively run the ball, which then puts it all on the shoulders of a quarterback who, outside of the playoffs last year, has been exceptionally turnover-prone. That then, in turn, puts way too much pressure on this defense. Then there's the Chiefs, a team that has a defense under Steve Spagnuolo that feels tailor-made to be able to put Darnold into turnover-prone positions in this game. Now, to be sure, the Kansas City passing offense hasn't been operating on all cylinders, so I do wonder what Mike Macdonald will have in store to try and bottle up Kenneth Walker III. At the end of the day, though, there's simply more I trust with the Chiefs right now than with Seahawks, so even on the road, give me KC. Easiest NFL Week 7 pick on the board New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Don't mistake this for having any type of unwavering faith in the New York Jets. It's wavering quite a bit. At the same time, maybe the thing that I'm most confident in right now is the fact that the Miami Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL. Yes, they might win a game randomly at some point this season, but I have a hard time believing that win comes on the road and that it comes against a team that is at least as healthy as the Jets are right now in this moment. The Dolphins don't have anyone that can cover Garrett Wilson or even Omar Cooper Jr. in the passing game, which should give Geno Smith some consistent options in the pass game, while Braelon Allen and the offensive line are getting the run game clicking. The defense is fine overall, but the pass rush against a team that's not without De'Von Achane leads me to believe that Malik Willis is going to have a tough time on Sunday. This feels almost too simple, but I can't pass it up. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) I know, I know, I know. My Bo Nix slander has gone entirely too far. I can hear you complaining about it now, and it's a fair point, because even after beating the Rams, I'm under no guise that the Cardinals are a high-quality football team. At the same time, though, Nix is playing like the worst quarterback in the NFL right now. Even as someone low on Nix, I didn't expect this type of dramatic dropoff with no real signs of things getting any better. The Cardinals defense is certainly a generous unit, but I don't know if Sean Payton or Nix himself have enough faith in the quarterback right now to fully take advantage of that. Moreover, the defense has, on the whole, been lesser than a year ago and has been quite banged up. While the ceiling of the Cardinals is low, I don't think that Jacoby Brissett is going to make the same back-breaking mistakes we saw Sam Darnold make on Thursday Night Football last week. This feels like a game that could end up being similarly weird to Arizona's win over the Rams this past week, and I'm not only taking the Cards against the spread in this matchup, but give me them to pull off the upset fully while playing at home. away.blurb: The injuries just continue to pile up for the Los Angeles Rams. During Thursday’s practice, wide receiver Puka Nacua left early and was listed as limited with a calf injury . While details weren’t immediately available, NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport reported on Friday morning that the injury is believed to be minor. Nacua has already missed two games this season with a groin/hip injury. When Nacua was out, it was Adams who stepped up in his place. With Adams set to miss the next six weeks, the Rams will be relying heavily on Nacua. If Nacua were to miss Sunday’s game, it would put the Rams’ offense in a very difficult spot. The offense would likely rely on Tutu Atwell, who previously stepped up in place of Nacua in 2024. Players like Konata Mumpfield and Jordan Whittington would be asked to step up as well, and the Rams could look at rookie CJ Daniels. Even with Nacua out, it wouldn’t be surprising to see the Rams bring up Brennan Presley from the practice squad. Given the Rams' injury luck over the last few weeks, they can certainly be relieved that Nacua’s calf injury doesn't appear to be serious. However, while the news surrounding Nacua is encouraging, his availability for Sunday remains uncertain. Given the inconsistencies on offense and Adams' absence, the Rams need Nacua available as they look to avoid dropping to 2-5. “My understanding is, after tests, it was more minor than anything else. I wouldn’t say precautionary, because it’s not nothing, but at least not a significant injury,” said Rapoport. What that doesn’t tell us is whether or not Puka Nacua would be able to play.” Rapoport mentioned that it’s safe to say that Nacua’s status is up in the air for Sunday. After placing a handful of players such as wide receiver Davante Adams and defensive lineman Kobie Turner on injured reserve this week , the Rams were hoping to go into Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders as healthy as possible. The Rams took significant hits on defense this week as Turner was placed on injured reserve along with Poona Ford. Additionally, cornerback Trent McDuffie has not practiced at all this week after injuring his groin last Thursday. Remaining as healthy as they can on the offensive side of the ball as Adams and Terrance Ferguson recover from injuries will be essential to keeping the offense competitive over the next several weeks. The Rams will get information on Nacua later on Friday when the team reports to practice. Nacua will unlikely be a full participant, but head coach Sean McVay should at least be able to provide some more details. home.headline: Bills' Sam Franklin Jr. Suspended by NFL for Spitting at Raiders, Joins CJGJ in Missing Week 8
home.blurb: Buffalo Bills defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. landed in some hot water for an incident during the team's Week 6 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. The NFL announced that Franklin has been suspended for one game for "an act of unsportsmanlike conduct" after he was seen spitting at an opponent in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game. The Bills are on a bye this week, so Franklin will miss their Week 8 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Franklin "is denying the allegation and will appeal." Franklin joined the Bills' practice squad prior to the 2025 season and quickly earned a spot on the main roster. He appeared in all 17 games last season, mostly on special teams. He was voted a team captain this season. While Franklin is denying the allegation, it seems like the Bills had a hard time keeping their mouths shut during Sunday's contest. Veteran safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson also received a one-game suspension after cameras caught him spitting toward Raiders tight end Brock Bowers and center Tyler Linderbaum. "C.J. knows that it's hard enough to win in this league with 48 guys, much less 47. He knows that that can't happen. It's inexcusable. That's not the standard that we're going to have and play with," Bills head coach Joe Brady told reporters on Monday. "He's addressed it. It's been addressed. The league came down with the suspension. … We want to toe the line with everything we do but we can't cross the line." Gardner-Johnson addressed the incident with his teammates and coaches after the game, and he posted an apology for his actions on social media. "My passion and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed," he wrote. "The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game." The Bills will try to focus on avoiding any further incidents during their bye week before returning to action on Nov. 1 against the Ravens.

home.headline: Rams WR Puka Nacua leaves practice early with calf injury, status uncertain for Raiders game
home.blurb: "I think they're going to give it a couple of days and figure out exactly when is the best time," McVay added. "It's more of a cleanup type of procedure. There is a surgery, but it's a cleanup. I'm not a doctor so I don't want to speak out of turn, but it will be something that'll get cleaned up." The Rams were already looking for ways to get Nacua more involved after he saw limited opportunities against Arizona. McVay attributed his reduced involvement to the offense's inability to sustain drives. "We didn't have a lot of plays," McVay said. "Then there was a lot of lack of consistency in terms of sustaining drives. The snaps were limited and that's probably what went into it." The injuries have forced McVay and general manager Les Snead to consider not only their immediate roster needs but also how to manage the limited number of players who can return from injured reserve during the season. "I try not to live that way," McVay said when asked whether he comes to work expecting more bad injury news. "I think what you have to do is you have to deal with these different types of things. The first thing is you feel bad for the guys that are affected by things that oftentimes are out of their control. Then the next thing is let's be able to deal with it. The game's coming on Sunday." For McVay, the immediate priority is keeping his team focused on preparation rather than the growing list of players unavailable to contribute. "There are a lot of different things that have gone on but I'm grateful for the opportunity to be able to continue to coach this team," McVay said. "I want to make sure that they feel that gratitude that I have. It doesn't mean you lack empathy for the people that are being affected by it. You wish they were available." The Rams will now wait for additional information on Nacua's calf injury before determining whether their top remaining receiving threat will be available Sunday. They will compete in a Sunday Night Football matchup for the second time in 2026 as they head to Seattle to take on the reigning Super Bowl champions. While Andy Reid's squad has yet to drop a game, the Seahawks have struggled to get their offense going in the post-Kenneth Walker era . Amid their two-game losing streak, quarterback Sam Darnold has tossed four interceptions, including one that ultimately gave the Broncos a free victory last week in overtime. Sportsbooks have labeled Seattle as a slight home favorite, but what does the ESPN Matchup Predictor think? Here's what their computer model projects a few days before kickoff. Chiefs on SI's Take Usually, the matchup predictor closely mirrors what traditional betting lines are forecasting. However, that isn't the case for this contest. This was undoubtedly circled as one of the more difficult challenges on the Chiefs' schedule heading into the season, and that stands true despite Seattle's early shortcomings. They have the same defensive playmakers who made them a force to be reckoned with in last year's postseason. Even with Darnold's inconsistencies through the air, Jaxon Smith-Njigba remains a premier wide receiver in the league. He leads the NFL in receptions, receiving yards, and receiving touchdowns in spite of the shaky quarterback play. Seattle's passionate 12s will undoubtedly come out in full force, as this game means a lot more to them than it does to the Chiefs. Kansas City obviously wants to preserve its flawless record, but a loss that drops Seattle to 3-4 would likely take the Seahawks out of the division race moving forward. Walker's homecoming to the team he spent his first four years with is a major storyline. He'll be looking to prove why Seattle should have paid him as he continues to establish himself as one of the best running backs in the NFL. The Chiefs have had plenty of breaks go their way and won't stay undefeated forever, but the Seahawks will have a tough time overcoming turnovers from Darnold if they want to win. Unlike some of their past opponents, Patrick Mahomes will make them pay. Kenneth Walker III returns to his old stomping grounds on Sunday Night Football when the Kansas City Chiefs face the Seattle Seahawks in Week 7. Walker, now the NFL's leading rusher with Kansas City, faces his former team as Seattle enters as a home favorite of less than a field goal. My Chiefs vs. Seahawks predictions don't doubt Walker's desire to stick it to his former club, but my NFL picks won't discount the Super Bowl champs on Oct. 25. TOP Pick Chiefs vs Seahawks prediction: Seahawks moneyline The Seattle Seahawks have had a week and a half to stew over what could have been last Thursday. Seattle outplayed Denver in a challenging short-week trip to the thin air of Mile High, but three turnovers left the Seahawks with a 17-14 loss despite outgaining Denver by 186 yards. The Seahawks are rested and ready with the infamous 12 on their side on Sunday night, presenting a much stiffer test for the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs . Kansas City hasn't run into a defense as good as Seattle's. Outside of a Week 1 win over the Broncos, the Chiefs have bullied defensive units currently ranked 21st or worse in Defensive DVOA. Seattle sits No. 2 in that popular advanced metric , and its four-man front is the reason why I'm taking the home team to win outright. The Seahawks are generating the second-highest pressure rate despite Mike Macdonald blitzing on fewer than 24% of opponent dropbacks. Seattle is No. 1 in ESPN's pass rush win rate , boasting 16 sacks and 30 QB hits . Whenever we've seen Patrick Mahomes struggle, it's been against opponents capable of generating that level of pressure with just a four-man rush. Mahomes' 2026 PFF offensive grade drops from 90.6 when kept clean to 64.8 under duress . Chiefs vs Seahawks combo The Seahawks have the rest and home edge, bringing the best defense the Chiefs have faced all season. Holani's TD markets are being discounted due to Charbonnet's possible return, but he should still get his share of touches in the second half. Zach Charbonnet is trending toward playing his first game for Seattle since injuring his knee in the postseason last year. That's shaking up the TD markets for running backs Emanuel Wilson and George Holani . Holani scored his first touchdown last week and was the Seahawks' weapon of choice in the second half, leading Seattle's RBs with a 58% snap share . On the season, Holani has eight red-zone carries and is the third-down option, with two receptions inside the 20-yard line. picks.headline: Seahawks Get Devastating News on Former 2nd-Round Pick Before Chiefs Game
picks.blurb: Seahawks Get Devastating News on Former 2nd-Round Pick Before Chiefs Game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview Seahawks Get Devastating News on Former 2nd-Round Pick Before Chiefs Game SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 30: Elijah Arroyo #18 of the Seattle Seahawks reacts to a play in the third quarter of a game against the Minnesota Vikings at Lumen Field on November 30, 2025 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jane Gershovich/Getty Images) Getty Duncan Day Thu, October 22, 2026 at 9:08 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Elijah Arroyo #18 of the Seattle Seahawks is assisted off the field after a play against the Denver Broncos during the second quarter of the game at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) Getty SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 11: AJ Barner #88 of the Seattle Seahawks catches the ball against the San Francisco 49ers at Lumen Field on October 17, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty The Seattle Seahawks have suffered a season-ending injury blow to one of their promising young offensive weapons. Second-year tight end Elijah Arroyo is undergoing shoulder surgery Thursday, Oct. 22, and will miss the remainder of the 2026 season. ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter reported the development Thursday, delivering a disappointing verdict on Seattle's former second-round draft pick. "Source: Seahawks TE Elijah Arroyo is undergoing shoulder surgery today and will miss the rest of the season," Schefter wrote. The announcement comes just three days before Seattle hosts the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs in a highly anticipated Sunday Night Football matchup. It also marks a significant reversal from earlier expectations that Arroyo might return following a relatively brief absence. Seahawks Lose Arroyo for Rest of 2026 Season GettyDENVER, COLORADO – OCTOBER 15: Elijah Arroyo #18 of the Seattle Seahawks is assisted off the field after a play against the Denver Broncos during the second quarter of the game at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) Arroyo suffered the shoulder injury during Seattle's 17-14 loss to the Denver Broncos on October 15. The 23-year-old exited during the second quarter and was initially listed as doubtful to return. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald revealed the following day that Arroyo was undergoing further examination to determine the severity of the injury. "He's getting some imaging and testing as we speak, so no update yet," Macdonald said, per the team's official website . ESPN's Jeremy Fowler subsequently reported October 19 that Arroyo was likely headed to injured reserve, which would require him to miss at least four games. That outlook has now changed dramatically. Rather than potentially returning for Seattle's late-season push, Arroyo will spend the remainder of the campaign recovering from surgery. The setback is particularly frustrating considering his draft pedigree. Seattle selected the former Miami standout with the No. 50 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft following a breakout collegiate season in which he recorded 35 receptions, 590 yards and seven touchdowns. Arroyo flashed potential as a rookie, catching 15 passes for 179 yards and one touchdown across 13 regular-season appearances. A knee injury interrupted his debut campaign and sidelined him for the final four regular-season games, although he eventually returned for Seattle's championship-winning postseason run. His second season offered an opportunity to build on that foundation. Instead, Arroyo managed just one reception for 17 yards in 2026 before his latest injury brought the season to a premature conclusion. Seahawks Have Tight End Decision Following Arroyo Injury GettySEATTLE, WASHINGTON – OCTOBER 11: AJ Barner #88 of the Seattle Seahawks catches the ball against the San Francisco 49ers at Lumen Field on October 17, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Arroyo's absence leaves Seattle without a young pass-catching option who was expected to develop into a larger contributor. Fortunately for the Seahawks, AJ Barner remains established as the team's starting tight end. Barner has recorded 15 receptions for 138 yards through six games this season. He finished 2025 with 52 catches, 519 yards and six touchdowns. Veteran Eric Saubert and Nick Kallerup also provide depth at the position. Seattle had already taken steps to reinforce the group before Schefter's announcement. On Monday, Oct. 19, the Seahawks signed veteran tight end Josiah Deguara to their practice squad. Deguara, a former third-round selection by the Green Bay Packers , has appeared in 78 NFL games with 12 starts. He has accumulated 53 receptions for 471 yards and three touchdowns during his career. Whether Seattle makes another move following Arroyo's season-ending diagnosis remains to be seen. For now, the immediate challenge is preparing for Kansas City without the young tight end. The Seahawks enter Sunday's matchup at 3-3 following consecutive losses to Denver and the San Francisco 49ers . With Arroyo unavailable, Seattle will have to lean on its remaining tight ends as the team attempts to reverse that slide and regain ground in the NFC West. away.headline: Chiefs’ Latest Injury Report Raises Concerns About Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice, and Four Others Before Seahawks Game
away.blurb: According to the Chiefs’ official X account, “Travis Kelce, Cooper McDonald, L’Jarius Sneed, and Brashard Smith were limited in practice today. Jaylon Moore and Rashee Rice did not practice.” The Week 7 injury report highlighted that right tackle Jaylon Moore and wide receiver Rashee Rice did not participate in Wednesday and Thursday’s practices, while tight end Travis Kelce, linebacker Cooper McDonald, and cornerback L’Jarius Sneed remained limited. Besides them, running back Brashard Smith, who is also dealing with a hamstring, was held to limited on Thursday’s practice. WR Rashee Rice , who sustained a hamstring injury in Week 4, still remains ‘Questionable’ to play this Sunday as lingering issues prevented him from joining practice sessions ahead of their Seahawks clash. Travis Kelce, who tweaked his right ankle in the first quarter of the Week 6 game, is also ‘Questionable’ to play. After Kelce managed to return to the game and score four receptions for 53 yards on October 18. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid relayed the news that Kelce was going to be okay, albeit with some soreness in his ankle. But at 37 years old, it is still unclear whether the veteran tight end would be cleared this week. Both offensive tackles Josh Simmons and Jaylon Moore remained absent from practice on Wednesday. Moore suffered a concussion during the second quarter of the Week 6 Chargers game and was ruled out for the remainder of the game. After the diagnosis was confirmed, the tackle entered the NFL’s five-step concussion protocol. Meanwhile, Simmons, who had been struggling with a herniated disk in his lower back since August, was put on Injured Reserve again on Thursday, delaying his return. Simmons was selected by Kansas City with the 32nd overall pick of the 2025 draft. It was hoped he would become their franchise left tackle. home.blurb: Look, this injury hurts because Elijah Arroyo was just starting to carve out a role. The Seahawks took him in the second round of the 2025 NFL draft with the 50th overall pick. He bounced back and put together a great college career with the Hurricanes, which is a big reason Seattle used a second-round pick on him. Seahawks tight end Elijah Arroyo will miss the rest of the 2026 season, dealing another significant blow to his development after previous injury setbacks. How much more can Elijah Arroyo’s young career take? The Seattle Seahawks tight end is undergoing shoulder surgery and will miss the rest of the 2026 season, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter . Arroyo got hurt in last Thursday night’s primetime loss to the Denver Broncos as he was trying to recover a fumble by wide receiver Rashid Shaheed. It’s a brutal way to lose a season, and it’s even tougher for a second-year player who still has a lot to prove. The numbers tell the story. Arroyo will miss 11 games for Seattle, plus any potential postseason run. Seahawks fans won’t see him on the field again until 2027. Arroyo’s development takes a hit As a rookie, he played in 13 games and caught 15 passes for 179 yards and one touchdown. Those aren’t eye-popping numbers, but they’re a reasonable foundation for a first-year tight end learning the NFL game. The 2026 season hasn’t gone the way anyone hoped, though. Through six games, Arroyo had just one catch for 17 yards, obviously much less production than his rookie year. Now he won’t get the chance to turn that around. This shoulder injury is going to set him back a good bit. A second-year jump matters for young tight ends, and Arroyo loses most of that year. Losing those reps hurts. Injury history follows Arroyo from Miami to Seattle Now, Arroyo’s injury history isn’t new . It just hasn’t involved his shoulder until now. Most of his problems have been with his knee. The knee issues followed him to the NFL, though. In December 2025, Arroyo suffered a Grade One knee strain. It resulted in the Seahawks placing him on injured reserve, and him missing the rest of the season. This shoulder injury is a different animal for Elijah Arroyo. It’s the longest absence of his pro career by a wide margin. For a player who has already lost chunks of time in college and the NFL, it’s another frustrating hurdle. The Seahawks are set at the position with AJ Barner leading the way. Seattle’s passing game will keep running through its top options, and the tight end room isn’t suddenly in crisis mode. The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The Niners have been excellent against the run this year, and if this game winds up being one where Penix has to match Purdy throw for throw, I don't see that going well for Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Falcons 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens (-3) Dajani ( Bengals +3): The Bengals are fresh off their bye while the Baltimore Ravens are fresh off ... a loss to the Cleveland Browns . It was their 15th loss when leading by at least seven points in the fourth quarter since 2020, which ranks the most in the NFL. Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this week, but I'm curious to see how "spry" he looks. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr. are the only defensive tackle trio to record multiple sacks this season. … Prediction: Bengals 29, Ravens 27 Dubin (Ravens -3): I'm assuming that Lamar Jackson is back for this game. If he's not, then you can switch my pick to the Bengals. If Jackson is in alongside Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers , I just don't think this Baltimore offense can be stopped. When those three have shared the field this season, the Ravens are averaging 9.9 yards per play. NINE POINT NINE. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. If there is any team that can compete with an explosive offense, it's probably the Bengals, but I don't see them quite keeping up here. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bengals 26 Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani ( Lions -3): Just take the Over in this matchup. The Lions really burned me coming off the bye last year, losing to J.J. McCarthy , but I'm going to back them in this spot. The concern is, of course, the defense, which ranks dead last in the NFL with 404.4 total yards surrendered per game. HOWEVER, I will mention that Kelvin Sheppard 's unit forced five straight three-and-outs from the Cardinals in that 45-21 win in Week 5. Plus, Brian Branch is set to return to the lineup as well. Give me the Lions at home. … Prediction: Lions 35, Packers 30 Dubin (Lions -3): This one has all the makings of a shootout, with two explosive offenses going back and forth. Jared Goff and Co. are coming off the bye, and they have scored 31 or more points in four of their five games to date — and they scored 26 while piling up 452 yards in the other one. Nobody except maybe Kenneth Walker III is doing it at a higher level than Jahmyr Gibbs right now, either. Meanwhile, Green Bay can throw the ball all over the yard, and everyone throws it on the Lions. Maybe Green Bay can actually run with some efficiency in Josh Jacobs ' potential return, but it's not like he was all that efficient last season, either. I lean toward the Lions because they can beat you both ways. … Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 28 Kansas City Chiefs at Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) (SNF) Dajani (Chiefs +2.5): The Seahawks looked completely disinterested in that Week 6 loss to the Denver Broncos . Before the season started, this looked like a potential swing game for the NFC East standings, but a lot has changed in six weeks. Dallas is off to a slow start at 2-4, and the defense (31st in EPA/Play) remains one of the worst in the NFL. Dak Prescott and Co. have lost back-to-back primetime games against Tampa Bay (Week 5) and Green Bay (Week 6), looking pretty rough in both appearances. So, can they turn things around on the road against a divisional opponent? The Eagles enter this game on a four-game losing streak, and star quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots in his lungs. That is a massive blow to the Eagles in the futures market, as they’re now last in the odds to win the NFC East and +15000 to win the Super Bowl. Tanner McKee is set to make another start in Week 7, and this may turn into a lost season for an Eagles team that could decide to trade some veteran pieces to recoup draft capital and lighten the load on the salary cap in years to come. Oddsmakers have set the Cowboys as favorites in this matchup, and a win would put Dallas in a much better position to win the NFC East – which it is still favored to do. Here’s a look at the odds, the latest movement since Sunday night and a quick preview of this primetime matchup. Cowboys vs. Eagles Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Cowboys -4.5 (-112) Eagles +4.5 (-108) Cowboys: -225 44.5 (Over -110/Under -110) Dallas opened as a 5.5-point favorite for Monday night’s showdown , but that line has quickly shifted towards the Eagles. Even with Jalen Hurts on injured reserve and out for the season, Philly has a shot to pull off an upset against a Dallas defense that is 31st in the NFL EPA/Play. Plus, the Cowboys’ offense looked awful on Sunday night in a loss to Green Bay, which may have caused the move in this line on Monday morning. Cowboys vs. Eagles Betting Preview The Eagles have covered the spread just once in the 2026 season (in their London loss to Jacksonville), so it’s hard to justify betting on them with a backup at quarterback. However, Dallas’ defense remains a bottom three unit in the league, and McKee (215 passing yards in Week 6) was at least able to move the Philly offense. If Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is able to return in Week 7, it could flip these odds even further towards the Eagles. Dallas needs to figure things out on offense, as Prescott has struggled with turnovers (not all his fault) in the last few games while the offensive line allowed him to take a ton of big hits in Week 6. A win for Philly could bump it back up into at least the No. 3 spot in the odds to win the NFC East, but it seems pretty clear that oddsmakers expect Dallas to eventually figure things out and advance as the division winner. Bettors may want to consider the OVER (44.5) with how poor the Dallas defense has been this season. The OVER is 4-2 in Dallas’ six games and 3-3 in the Eagles’ matchup in 2026. away.headline: Cowboys' preseason superstar could make NFL debut thanks to KaVontae Turpin injury
away.blurb: The Cowboys have carried five receivers into gamedays for every contest this season. Turpin being ruled out would lessen that number to four, unless they dress Camden Brown, who has remained inactive for every game this season. DeMarvion Overshown Injury Update: Cowboys Star LB Could Return in Week 6 The Dallas Cowboys are dealing with an injury at wide receiver that opens the door for one of the team's preseason superstars to make his NFL debut in Week 7. That injury is to wide receiver and returner KaVontae Turpin, who is dealing with a ribs injury he suffered in Week 6. Turpin did not take part in practice on Thursday. Furthermore, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports that Turpin is dealing with "cartilage damage" and will "probably" miss at least this week, when the Cowboys face the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night. "Cowboys receiver/returner KaVontae Turpin suffered an injury to his ribs Sunday, and one source believes he's dealing with cartilage damage," Fowler wrote. "He will probably miss this week and go from there," he added. Dallas' offense has sputtered of late . Perhaps the Cowboys should not only dress Brown, who was electric during the preseason, but also give him some snaps. Brown also has special teams experience after playing in that area during the preseason, so that gives him added value and a better chance to finally see the field in Week 7. Camden Brown's electric offseason An undrafted free-agent signing of the Cowboys after the 2026 NFL Draft, Brown was a menace against Dallas defense in camp (that doesn't hold as much weight as it once did with how badly the Cowboys' defense has played, but I digress) and he then carried that into the preseason with electric showings. The 6-foot-2, 204-pound wide receiver tallied three catches for 62 yards and two touchdowns in preseason Week 1 , and followed that up with two catches for 77 yards in the second exhibition contest. “The game’s not too big for him. He does it every day in practice, we see it all the time," head coach Brian Schottenheimer stated . "Really good day, but he’s got to keep stacking what he’s been doing." But it wasn't just about the totals for Brown, who made some "this guy belongs in the league" kinds of catches along the way. Brown cooled off in the final preseason game with just one catch for 27 yards, but he had done enough to state his case and the Cowboys ended up keeping him against all odds because the expectation all offseason was the team would only carry five wideouts with how top-heavy it was. Cowboys fans have been wanting to see Brown all season long after the impressive display he had during the offseason. With Turpin likely to sit, it's time to free Camden Brown and let him play some snaps on offense, too. home.headline: NFL Fans Demand 'Investigation' Into Philadelphia Eagles' Medical Staff
home.blurb: NFL Fans Demand 'Investigation' Into Philadelphia Eagles' Medical Staff - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Andrew Holleran Mon, October 19, 2026 at 2:49 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Eagles are likely to be without star quarterback Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season, as he's being put on blood thinners, the team announced on Monday. Hurts missed this past Sunday's game after being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot. He had previously played in a loss to the Jaguars in London earlier this month. "Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition. Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. 'blood thinners'). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football," the team announced. "Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners.
